scenes.synopsis: open the season — the assembly's aftermath; the war ended, the atelier scarred; the cost, counted. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Dawn at Hartwell Park, and the first morning that belongs to nobody else. The war is over — Cecilia gone from London, the atelier scarred in the saving, Élise safe upstairs with her sketchbook. Rose stands at the window in her dressing gown and takes stock of the quiet the way a general walks a field after the guns stop: counting what held, counting what broke, and finding, to her surprise, that the house still smells of beeswax and rain.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The light comes in grey and plain, and it shows everything: the garden beds put back in order, the gravel raked, the park's green shouldering up out of the mist as if the last year never happened.* — remembered: *Mist lifting over the beds.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She allows herself one unguarded minute to be glad. Then she puts the gladness away with the other luxuries, and opens the account book of the war in her head.* — remembered: *One minute of gladness, then the ledger.*
> (T3 · stance) *Warrior first, heiress second: that is the order she won it in, and she will keep it in that order. The house did not save itself; she did, with her own hands and other people's courage.* — remembered: *Warrior first; the order holds.*
> (T4 · tone) *Dry, even this early, even alone. "Well," she says to the empty room, "that was a year." The room, sensibly, offers no opinion.* — remembered: *Dry already, even at dawn.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The scars are there if she looks for them: the atelier's beams still smell of smoke when the sun hits them, and the new wood stands out paler against the old like a stammer in a sentence.* — remembered: *New wood paler than old.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She walks the corridor slowly, touching each doorframe as she passes, the way she used to as a child. The house lets itself be touched. That, she decides, is forgiveness enough for one morning.* — remembered: *Touching her way down the corridor.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *Élise is safe. That was the price and the prize both, and it is paid in full. Everything else — the money, the gossip, the repairs — is arithmetic.* — remembered: *Paid in full, both ways.*
> (T8 · choice) *She chooses the morning: to stand in it, unhurried, before the world remembers she exists. The war is filed. What comes next has not yet knocked.* — remembered: *Unhurried, before the knocking starts.*
> *(She dresses without ringing for anyone, which feels like a small declaration of independence. Below stairs, the kitchen is already clattering. The house has resumed its business, and she means to resume hers — whatever, this morning, that turns out to be.)*
> *The sun comes up over the park, and Rose Hartwell, twenty-five and undefeated, goes down to breakfast.*

scenes.synopsis: Letitia's report — the household's state; the war's end, the aunt's way. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The breakfast room, and Letitia already entrenched behind the toast rack with the expression of a woman who has been awake since five out of pure professional curiosity. The war's accounts are to be settled over kedgeree, and the Hawk has brought her own ledger: gossip, mostly, but itemized.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *Letitia's cap is slightly crooked, which means she dressed in a hurry, which means she has news. Rose pours the tea and waits. The Hawk hates to be asked; she loves to be watched waiting.* — remembered: *Reading the cap, not the face.*
> "Over, darling." Letitia seizes a piece of toast. "Properly over. Cecilia's boxes went to the carrier yesterday, and the hall porter at her lodgings told my girl the trunks were labeled for the north. The north! One pictures wolves." — Letitia
> (T2 · tone) *"One pictures her arguing with the wolves about precedence," Rose says, and Letitia laughs so hard she has to put the toast down.* — remembered: *Toast down; that laugh is real.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *"And the atelier, darling? The scars?" Letitia leans forward. "Are they the sort of scars a girl boasts about in company, or the sort one covers with a shawl?"* — remembered: *Boast or shawl — the question stands.*
> "The boasting sort," Rose says. "The beams held. The work held. Élise is upstairs drawing as if nothing happened, which is the bravest thing I have seen all year." — Rose
> (T4 · stance) *Letitia pats her hand with uncharacteristic gentleness. "Then we drink to the scars, darling. Honorable scars. The kind that improve one."* — remembered: *Honorably scarred, and drinking to it.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *The morning post sits unopened beside Letitia's plate, and the Hawk keeps glancing at it sideways. Curiosity, in Letitia, is a physical itch.* — remembered: *She cannot not look.*
> "Open it, then," Rose says. "You know you will read the directions through the paper if I don't." — Rose
> (T6 · look closer) *"A woman of business must know the mails," Letitia says with dignity, slitting a seal. "It is practically a profession."* — remembered: *Slitting seals with dignity.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *Rose watches her aunt work through the pile — bill, invitation, bill, circular — and feels the morning settle into its familiar shape. The war may be filed, but the Hawk's accounting never closes.* — remembered: *The morning settling into shape.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *"Nothing that bites," Letitia announces, tossing the last letter aside. "We are solvent, invited, and unbitten. Drink your tea, darling."* — remembered: *Filed under unbitten.*
> *(The kedgeree is excellent, the tea is hot, and for one whole breakfast the world behaves as though a quiet life were a thing a Hartwell might actually be allowed. Rose knows better, and eats anyway.)*
> *Letitia refills both cups, and the morning proceeds on the pleasant fiction that nothing is about to happen.*

scenes.synopsis: Augusta's counsel — the war's cost, the Dowager's way; the pearls, mentioned. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room, and Augusta enthroned by the window with her spectacles on and the household accounts spread before her like a battle map. The Dowager does not do sentiment before noon; she does arithmetic, which in her hands is the same thing, only sharper.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The pencil taps twice against the ledger — Augusta's full stop. "The war," she says, "is paid for. Sit down, Rose. I have done the reckoning, and you will hear it whether you like it or not."* — remembered: *Two taps: the full stop.*
> (T2 · tone) *"The atelier stands. Élise stands. You stand." Augusta removes her spectacles. "Cecilia does not stand in London, which is the only column that matters. It was expensive. It was also correct."* — remembered: *Expensive, and correct.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose sits. When Augusta uses that voice, the furniture itself seems to sit straighter. "I know it was expensive, Grandmama."* — remembered: *Sitting straighter with the furniture.*
> (T4 · stance) *"Expensive is a word for people who cannot afford things," Augusta says. "We could afford it. Barely. The distinction matters." The spectacles go back on. The distinction, Rose understands, is the whole of the Dowager's philosophy: that a Hartwell may be ruined by anything except being unable to pay for the ruining.* — remembered: *Ruined by anything but the bill.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *Outside the window, a gardener is replanting the border Cecilia's carriage once churned to mud. Augusta watches him the way she watches everything: as evidence. "He has been at it since Tuesday," she observes. "The mud remembers longer than the town does."* — remembered: *Watched like evidence.*
> (T6 · look closer) *"You fought well," Augusta says, not looking at her. It is the nearest thing to praise she has offered in a year, and Rose takes it carefully, the way one takes a hot dish.* — remembered: *The nearest thing to praise.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She will not preen; Augusta would notice, and the pencil would tap. She folds her hands and says, "Thank you," and means the whole of it. The Dowager nods once, the ledger already half-closed, the audience nearly over — and Rose understands that the thank-you has been accepted the way a correctly ruled column is accepted: without comment, which is the highest form of it.* — remembered: *Accepted without comment.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *"Now," Augusta says, closing the ledger with a soft thump, "we get on with being rich and respectable, which is harder than war and pays worse. Ring for more tea." The bell is rung, the cold cup removed, and the morning room prepares itself for the next item of business, whatever it proves to be.* — remembered: *Harder than war, worse paid.*
> *(The tea comes, strong enough to stand a spoon in, and the morning room settles into its peacetime rhythm. Augusta's reckoning is filed alongside the war: counted, priced, and closed.)*
> *Rose drinks her tea, and the house exhales around her like a dog settling by the fire.*

scenes.synopsis: Élise and the atelier — the scars, the mending; the most disciplined work, foreshadowed. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The atelier, mid-morning: the smell of fresh-cut wood laid over the ghost of smoke, and Élise at the cutting table with her sleeves rolled and a pencil behind her ear. The workshop bears its scars the way soldiers bear theirs — visibly, and without apology.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The new beam runs paler across the ceiling, and the floorboards near the door are replacements, lighter than their neighbors. Élise has chalked a small flower on one of them, a private joke with the disaster.* — remembered: *Chalk on new boards: her joke.*
> (T2 · tone) *"Miss," Élise says, looking up, "the new silk came. Come and feel it." There is no tremor in her voice. Whatever the war took from her, it did not take her hands.* — remembered: *Her hands have no tremor.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose crosses to the table and runs the silk through her fingers. It is the color of rain on stone. "It will do beautifully," she says, and Élise's whole face changes the way a room changes when a lamp is lit.* — remembered: *A face like a lit lamp.*
> (T4 · stance) *The scarred wall has been left scarred — scorched boards framed, deliberately, by new ones. "We kept it," Élise says, following her gaze. "To remember the price. Also, it looks rather fine."* — remembered: *Old scars in new frames.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"It looks like a battle honor," Rose says. "Wear it like one." Élise laughs, and the sound fills the workshop the way music fills a church.* — remembered: *Hung on the wall like medals.*
> (T6 · look closer) *This was the cost that could not be counted in any ledger: a girl's safety, a girl's nerve, a girl's hands kept whole. It is paid. She will not revisit the price; she will honor the purchase.* — remembered: *Paid; the price stays closed.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *"Back to work, then, miss?" Élise asks, already reaching for the shears. "Back to work," Rose says. It is the finest sentence either of them knows.* — remembered: *Already reaching for the shears.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She stays an hour, pinning and praising and getting in the way, and leaves with chalk dust on her sleeve. The workshop hums behind her, scarred and singing.* — remembered: *The dust stays.*
> *(On the stairs down, Rose meets nobody, and is glad of it. Some rooms are chapels, and the atelier is hers: smoke and silk, the scar framed like a medal, a girl humming over her cutting.)*
> *The chalk dust stays on her sleeve all day, and she does not brush it off.*

scenes.synopsis: the letter — the lawyers' letter, delivered; the claim, the received. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Late morning, and the post comes up the drive the way trouble always comes to Hartwell Park: politely, on schedule, and in a hand she does not know. The letter is heavy, sealed twice, and franked from London. It sits on the silver tray like a guest who has arrived too early for the party.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The paper is solicitor's paper — thick, cream, expensive. The seal is a stranger's crest. Rose turns it over twice before she breaks it, reading the outside as if the inside might be postponed.* — remembered: *Reading the outside first.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *The tray waits. The footman waits. The whole house, she feels, is holding its breath in the walls. "Thank you," she says. "That will be all." Calm is a performance; she gives it well.* — remembered: *Calm, performed well.*
> (T3 · stance) *She carries the letter to the library unopened, because some things should be read sitting down and this has the weight of one of them. The library receives her with its usual indifference to drama.* — remembered: *Some letters need sitting down.*
> (T4 · tone) *Not yet. One more minute of not-knowing, while the morning is still ordinary. She sets the letter on the desk and looks out at the park instead.* — remembered: *One last ordinary minute.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The park is doing nothing in particular: rooks, sunlight, a gardener with a wheelbarrow. It has no idea a sealed letter is about to rearrange it. Rose envies it briefly.* — remembered: *The park knows nothing.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She breaks the first seal, then the second, the way one opens a door one has been told not to open. The paper unfolds with a crisp, legal sound.* — remembered: *Both seals broken.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *"Well," she says aloud, to no one, "here it is." The library declines to ask what it is. She begins to read.* — remembered: *Aloud, to no one.*
> (T8 · choice) *Half a page in, she stops, and goes back to the beginning, and reads it again more slowly. Some letters are read twice because they are loved. This one is read twice because it is loaded.* — remembered: *Twice read: loaded, not loved.*
> *(The letter is from a firm of solicitors. It speaks of an entail, of mortgages, of a cousin. It is courteous, precise, and utterly without hurry — the way a chess player moves when the trap has already closed.)*
> *Rose folds the letter along its creases, and the morning, which was ordinary a minute ago, is ordinary no longer.*

scenes.synopsis: Quill reads the letter — the claimant's name; the claim's shape, first stated. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Mr. Quill's chambers, that afternoon: the smell of old paper and older caution, and the solicitor himself behind his desk with the letter open before him like a patient on a table. He has read it three times. He reads it a fourth time while Rose watches, because thoroughness is his native language.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The chambers are exactly as they always are — the green-shaded lamp, the deed boxes ranked like soldiers, the clock that ticks slightly too loud. In times of trouble, Rose finds the furniture reassuring.* — remembered: *Furniture as reassurance.*
> "The entail, miss." Quill folds his hands. "The claim concerns the entail — broken, a generation ago, by your grandfather's hand. The mortgages raised upon the breaking. And the claimant." A pause. "Your cousin, miss. Mr. Hartwell." — Mr. Quill
> (T2 · tone) *"My cousin." Rose tastes the word. "I have a cousin." It comes out flatter than she intended; surprise, she is learning, has no manners.* — remembered: *The word 'cousin,' tasted flat.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *"A cadet branch, miss. Respectable. His late father's money went into the mortgages, year by year — the money that kept the Park standing." Quill's voice stays level, which is how she knows the ground is not.* — remembered: *Level voices mean unlevel ground.*
> "So he is owed a debt," Rose says slowly. "A debt, Mr. Quill — not the house." — Rose
> (T4 · stance) *"Precisely the question, miss." The solicitor permits himself the faintest inclination of the head. "A debt is one thing. The house is another. His solicitors appear to conflate them."* — remembered: *Refusing the conflation.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *Rackham's name surfaces in the papers — the old steward, his scattered notes. Quill taps the bundle with one finger. "Scattered, miss. But paper is paper."* — remembered: *Paper is paper.*
> (T6 · look closer) *"What do we do?" Rose asks. It is the first plain question she has asked all day, and Quill receives it the way a doctor receives a straight symptom: with professional relief.* — remembered: *The first plain question.*
> "We read everything, miss." Quill begins stacking the papers with small, exact movements. "Then we answer. The law rewards the thorough." — Mr. Quill
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She will be thorough. She will read until her eyes ache. Whatever this cousin wants, he will find the Hartwells prepared — or at least thoroughly informed.* — remembered: *Thorough, or nothing.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *"Then we begin tomorrow," she says, rising. "Thank you, Mr. Quill." The solicitor bows her out with the gravity of a man escorting a client into a long war.* — remembered: *A long war, begun politely.*
> *(The carriage ride home is quiet. Entail, mortgages, cousin: three words that were strangers this morning and are family by afternoon. Rose turns them over like stones, looking for the sharp edges.)*
> *Hugh Hartwell. Thirty, respectable, owed a debt. She says the name once, experimentally, and the carriage does not answer.*

scenes.synopsis: the letter's language — the lawyers' phrasing; the claim, the weighed. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, and the letter spread on the library desk under the lamp, read now so often the creases are going soft. Rose has made notes in the margins in pencil — small, neat, furious. The claim's paper, priced line by line.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *Three points, and no more: the entail was broken a generation ago — her grandfather's hand, to raise the mortgages. The mortgages were fed, year by year, with cadet-branch money. The cadet branch now claims the house for the debt.* — remembered: *Three points, no more.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *"Cheek," she says to the lamp. The lamp, being a lamp, agrees. It is pleasant, briefly, to be the only person in the room who is allowed an opinion. The portraits on the library wall offer none; the Hartwells in oil have faced worse than solicitors' letters, and their painted composure says so.* — remembered: *One opinion, permitted alone.*
> (T3 · stance) *But cheek is not an argument, and she knows it. She sits straighter and reads the third point again. A debt is owed — that much is honest. The house is another matter. She writes it in the margin in pencil, in plain English, because the plainness of it steadies her: a debt is not a house.* — remembered: *Plain English in the margin.*
> (T4 · tone) *Her grandfather broke the entail to save the estate. That was the sin, if sin it was: salvation by irregular means. She finds she cannot condemn it. The house stands; that is the defense and the verdict both.* — remembered: *Standing is the defense.*
> (T5 · look closer) *Rackham's scattered paper backs the cousin's claim — so Quill says. Scattered paper, old ink, a dead steward's notes. She will want to see every sheet before she believes a word of it. A steward's notes are only as honest as the steward, and Rackham has been dead too long to be cross-examined; the paper will have to speak for him.* — remembered: *Every sheet, before belief.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She writes three lines to Quill — read everything, copy everything, trust nothing yet — and seals it for the morning post. Action, even small action, steadies her.* — remembered: *Small action, taken fast.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *"A debt is not a house," she tells the empty library, practicing. It sounds well. It sounds like something a judge might underline. She tries it again, slower, the way she would say it standing up: "A debt is not a house."* — remembered: *Practicing for the judge.*
> (T8 · choice) *She folds the letter away in the desk, in the drawer where important things live. The claim is filed. Tomorrow, the answering begins.* — remembered: *The drawer of important things.*
> *(The house is quiet around her — the particular quiet of a place that has survived worse than solicitors' letters. Rose banks the lamp and goes upstairs, and the library keeps her notes like a promise.)*
> *A debt is not a house. She carries the sentence to bed like a candle.*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE RECEIVING (how to receive the claim: read it alone, read it with Quill, or read it with Augusta). The claim is received; decide before the claim decides for her. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library, evening: the letter read, the claim's shape understood, the cousin named. The question now is not what the claim says but how she receives it — and the receiving, Rose knows, is half the battle. She walks the carpet's length and prices the three roads: alone, with Quill, with Augusta.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The Receiving:*
- **Read it alone** — *the night's quiet, no witness.* She reads it again in the library's stillness — no witness to the first flinch, her own counsel first. (Consequence: the flinch stays hers alone — unwitnessed, unhurried; but counsel delayed is counsel weakened, and the night is long.)
- **Take it to Quill** — *the solicitor's reading, the professional.* She carries it back to the chambers in the morning — the law's first word, the professional's eye. (Consequence: the law speaks first — the claim met on its own ground; but the law's ground is paper, and paper favors whoever holds the most of it.)
- **Carry it to Augusta** — *the Dowager's reading, the family's.* She takes it to Augusta tonight — the Hartwell continuity weighed by its oldest keeper. (Consequence: the family's counsel — the oldest keeper reads it; but the Dowager reads the past, and the claim belongs to the present.)
> *(The choice goes into the ledger, and with it the manner of the choosing: the solitary reader, the solicitor's client, or the granddaughter. The claim was always going to be received. The signature — the how, the when, the with-whom — is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the household told — the war's end, the letter's coming; the kept, the informed. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The servants' hall, after dinner: the household assembled in its degrees — the housekeeper upright as a ruler, the footmen trying not to look interested, the maids frankly interested. News in a great house travels like weather; Rose has decided to be the sky it comes from.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *Forty-odd faces, and every one of them has heard something already. That is the nature of servants' halls: the postman talks to the groom, the groom talks to the cook, and by dinner the letter has been read by everyone except its recipient. She can see it in the way the maids sit forward and the footmen sit back — the two postures of people who already know, and are waiting to find out whether they know correctly.* — remembered: *The postman talked first.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps it plain and short. "There is a claim against the estate," she says. "A cousin, with solicitors. It will be answered properly, in the proper way. There is nothing to fear, and nothing to gossip about." The words land the way she intends them to: flat, factual, unadorned.* — remembered: *Nothing to fear, nothing to gossip.*
> (T3 · stance) *She stands while she says it — not behind a table, not enthroned, just standing among them. Rank has its uses, and one of them is showing up.* — remembered: *Standing, not enthroned.*
> (T4 · tone) *The housekeeper's nod is the one that matters, and it comes: once, decisive. The household will take its cue from her as it always does. The maids look relieved; the footmen look disappointed. Disappointment, in footmen, is the natural state when there is no scandal to polish into story — and Rose is careful to give them none.* — remembered: *The housekeeper's nod decides it.*
> (T5 · look closer) *"Questions?" Rose asks. There are none, which is the servants' hall's way of having a hundred. She nods. "Then back to work, and thank you."* — remembered: *Silence meaning a hundred.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She will tell them more when there is more to tell. A house kept in the dark invents its own candles, and the inventions are always worse than the truth.* — remembered: *Truth beats invention.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *"Miss looks tired," the housekeeper says quietly, as they file out. "Miss is fine," Rose says, and they both know it is a polite fiction, and they both honor it. The housekeeper's hand brushes her sleeve as she passes — the briefest touch, the whole of the below-stairs vocabulary for loyalty, and Rose feels it like a handrail on a dark stair.* — remembered: *The briefest of touches.*
> (T8 · choice) *She walks back through the quiet passages alone. The telling is done: the household knows what she knows, which is the most any of them can ask.* — remembered: *The telling is done.*
> *(Upstairs, the house settles. Somewhere a door closes softly. The telling has gone the way tellings go in well-run houses: into the walls, into the routine, into the keeping.)*
> *Rose finds she is hungry, and rings for supper, and the ordinary world resumes.*

scenes.synopsis: Octavia's counsel — the friend's reading; the studio, the unperforming room. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The gallery, late afternoon: the long wall of Hartwells looking down with their painted composure, and Octavia waiting by the newest portrait with her hands folded. Octavia does not fidget; she pauses, which is fidgeting refined to an art.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The portrait is Rose at twenty-four, painted the spring before the war: chin up, mouth unsmiling, the pearls not yet promised. Octavia studies it the way she studies everything — precisely, and without flinching.* — remembered: *Studied without flinching.*
> "You look tired, my love." Octavia does not turn around. "Tired is allowed. Defeated is not, and you are not defeated, so we will not discuss it." — Octavia
> (T2 · tone) *"I am not defeated," Rose says. "I am —" She searches for the word. "Sued, I think. There is a cousin. There are solicitors. It is all very legal."* — remembered: *Defeated is the wrong word.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *Octavia considers this with the gravity of a connoisseur. "A cousin is better than a stranger, my love. One can be rude to a cousin. It is practically expected."* — remembered: *One may be rude to cousins.*
> "The entail, Octavia." Rose joins her before the portrait. "My grandfather broke it. To save the house. And now the breaking has come home to roost." — Rose
> (T4 · stance) *"Then the house is the argument," Octavia says simply. "It stands. That is a better brief than most barristers get." She takes Rose's arm, and they walk the gallery's length together.* — remembered: *The house as brief.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *The painted Hartwells watch them pass — bewigged, beribboned, unanimous in their disapproval of the present. Rose has always suspected the ancestors of being smug.* — remembered: *Smug in oil.*
> (T6 · look closer) *"What will you do?" Octavia asks. It is the question everyone asks, and the first time it has not sounded like an accusation.* — remembered: *Asked, not accused.*
> "Answer it," Rose says. "Properly. Thoroughly. The way Quill answers everything — with paper, and patience, and no mistakes." — Rose
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She will not perform distress for her friends; distress is a currency, and she is saving hers. Octavia, precise as ever, asks for nothing she cannot give.* — remembered: *Saving her currency.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *They stop before the portrait again. "She looks like she could manage it," Octavia says, nodding at the painted Rose. "See that she does."* — remembered: *The painted Rose, instructed.*
> *(The gallery empties of afternoon, and the portraits dim to their evening brown. Rose walks back alone, and the painted chin goes with her like a reminder.)*
> *She could manage it. The portrait says so, and Octavia, and — on good days — the mirror.*

scenes.synopsis: Harrow consulted — the entail's first mention; the archive, the opened. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The estate office, morning: ledgers ranked to the ceiling, dust in the sunbeams, and James Harrow at his desk with sixty-one years of Hartwell history filed behind his spectacles. The living archive does not hurry; hurrying, in Harrow's experience, is how papers get mislaid.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *Harrow's desk is a landscape of exact piles, each squared at the corners. He finds the bundle Rose asks for without looking up from his tea — sixty-one years of practice in knowing where things are.* — remembered: *Finding it blind, by practice.*
> (T2 · tone) *"Your grandfather's hand, miss." Harrow lays a deed before her with the reverence of a priest. "I knew it well. A bold hand — wrote as if the ink were free."* — remembered: *Laid down like a sacrament.*
> "Bold," Rose says, "is one word for breaking an entail." She says it gently; Harrow served the grandfather, and loyalty outlives employers. — Rose
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *"Bold is the word he would have used himself, miss." Harrow's smile is thin but genuine. "He broke it to save the Park. Said a house standing irregularly was better than a ruin standing straight."* — remembered: *Irregular and standing.*
> (T4 · stance) *"Did he say that?" Rose leans forward. "Truly, Harrow — his own words?" "His own words, miss. I was in the room. I remember rooms."* — remembered: *He remembers rooms.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *The deed's signature sprawls across the page — the bold hand, the free ink. Rose traces it with her fingertip, feeling the dent the nib made in the paper forty years ago.* — remembered: *Fingertip in a forty-year dent.*
> (T6 · look closer) *"Will you swear to it?" she asks. "If it comes to swearing?" Harrow straightens, and sixty-one years stand up in him. "Miss," he says, "I will swear to anything I remember, and I remember everything."* — remembered: *Sworn on total recall.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She will treat his memory as gold and his paper as gospel, and she will write down everything he says before the day cools. Archives, even living ones, deserve clerks.* — remembered: *Clerking the living archive.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *"Then we begin with you," she says. "Tell me everything, Harrow — from the beginning, and slowly." The old man nods, and opens a ledger, and the past begins to speak.* — remembered: *The ledger opens; the past speaks.*
> *(They work till noon: deeds, letters, the steward's crabbed marginalia. Harrow's memory never falters; it merely pauses, the way a good horse pauses before a fence, and then goes on.)*

> - (T3) **The white muslin, starched** — *starch like armor, white like the lilies; purity as a public statement.*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE POSTURE (the claim's first posture: defiance, inquiry, or silence). The posture is chosen; decide before the town chooses it for her. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library, night: the claim's shape filed, the archive consulted, the face chosen. The question the night demands is the first one every defendant faces: what is her posture toward the claim? She walks the carpet and prices the three roads — defiance, inquiry, silence — the way a buyer prices horses: for wind, for temper, for what they will do under pressure.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The Posture:*
- **Defiance** — *the Hartwell name, stated whole.* She meets it head-on — the name stated entire, no flinch shown to the town. (Consequence: the town sees steel — the defendant's nerve priced in public; but steel invites the hammer, and the hammer is already raised.)
- **Inquiry** — *questions first, the paper hunted.* She meets it with questions — the hunt begun, the truth priced before the posture. (Consequence: the paper leads — the claim met on evidence; but evidence takes time, and the town decides quickly.)
- **Silence** — *nothing given, the dignity kept.* She meets it with nothing — the claim unanswered in public, the unmoved kept. (Consequence: the dignity holds — nothing to criticize, nothing to pity; but silence reads as fear to those who want it to.)
> *(The choice goes into the ledger, and with it the manner of the choosing: the defiant, the inquirer, or the silent. The defense was always going to begin. The signature — the stance, the temper, the first word — is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the mortgages from inside — the Park's books; the kept roof, the priced. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The estate office, afternoon: the Park's books spread across Harrow's great table, year by year, in plain ink. Mortgages' entries, payments, the cadet branch's money arriving like rain — regular, unremarked, keeping the roof on. The office smells of leather and dust and the faint iron of the ink, and the light through the high windows falls in slabs across the ledgers.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The columns run back forty years in Harrow's immaculate hand, and then in older hands before him. Money in, money out, interest, repairs: the estate's whole life reduced to figures, and the figures are honest.* — remembered: *Forty years, honestly figured.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *Here it is, the debt made visible: the late Mr. Hartwell's money, the cousin's father's, year by year into the mortgages. No flourish, no complaint — just entries, patient as rain. The sums are not large, taken singly; taken together, over forty years, they are the roof, the beams, the west wing's repointing — the house itself, bought in installments.* — remembered: *A house paid by installments.*
> (T3 · stance) *Rose follows the columns with her finger, year by year. The Park stood because this money came. That is a fact, and facts do not care whose side they are on.* — remembered: *Facts take no sides.*
> (T4 · tone) *She will not resent the money; resentment of a fact is a waste of posture. The debt is real. The house is also real. Both can be true.* — remembered: *She will not resent a fact.*
> (T5 · look closer) *A note in the margin, in Rackham's crabbed hand: paid in full, the quarter's interest. The old steward's satisfaction is visible in the underlining — three strokes, emphatic. She finds herself smiling at the dead man's pride; forty years on, the three strokes still say what he meant them to say: done, and done properly.* — remembered: *Three strokes: done properly.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *Harrow watches her read, saying nothing. When she looks up, he nods once — the nod of a man who has watched three generations learn the same lesson from the same books.* — remembered: *Watched by sixty-one years.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *"It is all here, Harrow," she says. "Every penny." "Every penny, miss," he agrees. "The books do not lie. That is their virtue and their failing."* — remembered: *Virtue and failing both.*
> (T8 · choice) *She closes the last ledger gently, the way one closes a door on a sleeping child. The money's story is learned. Tomorrow, she learns what it means.* — remembered: *Gently, like a door.*
> *(The office darkens around her as the sun moves off the windows. The books sit in their ranks, patient as ever, holding forty years of rain. Harrow trims the lamp without being asked, and the light comes up warm over the leather and the dust, and the Park's books keep their counsel — honest, unhurried, and complete.)*
> *Rose walks home through the park, and the house on the hill looks — for the first time — like something that was paid for.*

scenes.synopsis: the claim's ritual — dress the defendant for the law's eyes; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "The letter's week — the solicitor's chambers, the archive's rooms, the defendant's first appearances. The dress code of the defended: severe propriety — the law reads hems the way it reads exhibits. Nothing to criticize, nothing to pity. Serious colors permitted; the severity is the gown's whole argument. **Editorial criterion: respectability.**"
>
> **A. The Defendant** — the grey silk severe; the chambers', the unadorned. Motif: the ledger's ruling, restrained at cuff and hem — the reading, embroidered. Thread: **silver** (the reading, edged) / **dove silk** (the reading, matched) / **ivory whitework** (the reading, lit). Colorway: pearl grey + ash + silver. Accessories: the notebook in the reticule; the pencil behind the ear; grey kid gloves, plain.
> **B. The Heir** — the black bombazine plain; the archive, mourning's-edge. Motif: plainness, entire — the serious, unembroidered. Thread: **matching silk** (the serious, exact) / **jet** (the serious, edged) / **none** (the serious, plain). Colorway: black + jet + pearl grey. Accessories: the reticule, capacious; the gloves, plain; the jet brooch, small.
> **C. The Hartwell** — the white muslin starched; the lilies', the unassailable. Motif: the Hartwell oak, restrained — the continuity's, embroidered. Thread: **whitework** (the purity's, stated) / **silver** (the unassailable, edged) / **matching silk** (the starched, exact). Colorway: white + silver + pearl grey. Accessories: the white ribbon; pearl drop earrings; the notebook, the pencil; white kid gloves.
>
> *(The dressing room, the letter's morning: the solicitor's gown's week — the chambers, the archive, the law's eyes. She dresses the way the claim has dressed her: severe propriety, begun.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: the defendant, the heir, or the Hartwell — the claim's thesis, remembered. The hair, severe. The accessories, restrained. The mirror, to be consulted briefly. **Direction.** The letter's week — the solicitor's chambers, the archive's rooms, the defendant's first appearances. Dress to be unassailable. **Editorial criterion.** Respectability — every choice must answer the law's eyes, not the ballroom's.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the claim. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** the claim's face — the grey silk severe, or the black bombazine plain, or the white muslin starched — whichever the week chose, the respectability worn. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, exact:** the severe — no rustle for the chambers, no train for the archive's stairs. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** the work — reading's habit, the paper's. *5 coins.*
> *(The pins accumulate — the gown's line set, the work's sleeves — and the dressing room holds its morning light the way the library holds the paper: patiently.)*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, high:** the serious — the law takes the high for the respectable. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, coiled:** the braided — the severe, the kept. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Reticule, packed:** the notebook — pencil, behind-ear's spare. *5 coins.*
> *(The hair is severe, the reticule restrained — and the week leans in, the chambers waiting.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, plain:** the handling — paper handled, not displayed. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Boots, quiet:** the chambers' stairs — the archive's floors, the unheard. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Shawl, wool:** the morning — chambers' chill, the answered. *5 coins.*
> *(Quiet boots, plain gloves — the law's houses ask for the unheard, and she gives it.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, small:** the jet — serious, the unshowy. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** the severe — the chambers smell the paper, not the lady. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, straight:** the heir's — the Park defended by its mistress, the spine's. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine straightens — the heir's — and the mirror is consulted briefly from the corner of her eye.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, level:** the defendant's — met eye to eye, the counsel's table. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, even:** the reading — claim, answered. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, still:** the paper — handling, the reverent's. *5 coins.*
> *(Level gaze, even voice, still hands — the defendant's instruments, tuned for the law.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, measured:** the week — letter, worked. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, rare:** the defendant — week, priced. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Nod, once:** the solicitor's answer — the priced, the taken. *5 coins.*
> *(The step measured, the smile rare, the nod once — the chambers' own grammar, spoken fluently.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Turn, away:** the chambers' — the read, the remembered. *5 coins.*

scenes.synopsis: Julian's first word — the mended gloves; the lover's counsel, early. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The terrace, afternoon: Julian's first counsel — the mended gloves in her pocket, the claim's first question answered. He asks it the way he asks everything: plainly. What does the claim want? The house, or the acknowledgment of the money? The stone holds the afternoon's heat, and the question sits between them like a third person.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She takes the gloves out of her pocket — Élise's mending small and neat along the thumbs — and turns them in her hands while Julian waits. He has the patience of a man who has watched her do this since she was twelve.* — remembered: *Thumbs mended, gloves turned.*
> (T2 · tone) *"The house first, Julian," she says, dry as dust. "The money after — and then we shall see what the acknowledgment costs. The claim wants the house. It also wants the money named. It may not have both."* — remembered: *Dry as dust, and priced.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes the acknowledgment the way she takes everything now: priced before it is spoken, filed before it is answered. Let the cousin name his money. She will have named it first.* — remembered: *Before it is spoken, priced.*
> (T4 · stance) *As his cousin she stands acknowledged — his father's money is in the mortgages, and a debt is owed, though not the house. As his counsel she stands instructed — Julian's steadiness at her elbow, costing her nothing but the truth.* — remembered: *Cousin and counsel both.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Not yet," she says. "The word, when it's needed — you'll hear it." Julian nods. "The gloves' first word, cousin — priced, and spent when it must be." "Yours to hear," she tells him, "and yours to keep."* — remembered: *The word stays pocketed.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The stone is warm under her palm still, and below the terrace the park lies in its afternoon order — the drive, the gates, the London road like a held breath. All of it mortgaged, all of it standing. Hers to keep standing.* — remembered: *The park in afternoon order.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *He offers the name, the purse, the gloves — publicly, if it comes to it. She refuses them the way one refuses a loan from family: gently, and perhaps only for now. The counsel stays at her elbow. The gloves go back in the pocket.* — remembered: *Gently refused, for now.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She will take the counsel and leave the purse — Julian's steadiness costs nothing, and that is exactly what she will pay. The gloves stay in her pocket. The word stays in her keeping.* — remembered: *Counsel taken; purse left.*
> *(He offers everything and she takes nothing yet, and the terrace keeps its heat. The mended gloves wait in the pocket. The counsel waits at her elbow. The claim's first question has its answer, and the afternoon turns with the gloves' first word unspoken — and the promise, kept.)*
> *The stone cools, the gloves rest, and Rose goes in with the first word unspoken: the house, the money, the debt acknowledged.*

scenes.synopsis: the entail, explained — what breaking means; the law's history, the priced. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Mr. Quill's chambers, morning: what breaking means — the entail broken by her grandfather's hand, irregularly, to raise the mortgages; the estate failing, the money arriving, the roof staying on. The solicitor lays it out the way he lays out everything: as paper, with dates. The suggestion, not the proof. The hunt's true quarry gets its first name — the "other codicils," the predecessor's filing, wherever it is kept.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The solicitor's finger rests on the deed's margin, where her grandfather's hand broke the line. The paper is old. The break in it is older — and irregular, which is the kindest word the law owns.* — remembered: *The break predates the paper.*
> (T2 · tone) *"The money saved the estate, Mr. Quill," she says, sharp. "And the paper says so — where?" He inclines his head. "Broken, the entail," she adds, dry. "And the roof stayed on. Price the irregularity, solicitor, and answer it."* — remembered: *Pricing the irregularity.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes the irregularity the way she takes the weather: as a fact, and as the reason she is standing here. The estate was failing. The money came. The roof stayed on.* — remembered: *Weather, and the reason for standing here.*
> (T4 · stance) *As his client she stands instructed — the law's word on her grandfather's hand, and the price of hearing it. As the hunter she stands priced — the "other codicils" named at last, the predecessor's filing waiting wherever the predecessor kept his secrets.* — remembered: *Two stances, one solicitor.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Then the breaking stands, Mr. Quill — irregular, and standing. My grandfather broke the entail to save the estate, and I will not unbreak it to lose it."* — remembered: *Irregular, and standing.*
> (T6 · look closer) *"The suggestion, not the proof" — that is his phrase, and he weighs it like a coin on the blotter. The money entered the mortgages. The Park stood. Between those two facts lies the paper she must find.* — remembered: *Between two facts, the paper.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She meets his gravity with her full attention, the way one meets a man carrying something breakable. The chambers keep their morning. The paper keeps its break.* — remembered: *Attention for breakable things.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the quarry: the "other codicils," the predecessor's own phrase, the entail's true paper, filed wherever a careful man files what he does not wish found. The hunt has a name for what it seeks.* — remembered: *The hunt has a name.*
> *(She chooses the hunt. The chambers release her with the breaking priced — the entail broken and irregular, the money suggested as the saving of it, the proof unpromised, the quarry named. The morning turns with the paper broken — and the hunting, chosen.)*
> *The deeds rest, the finger lifts, and Rose walks out with the broken paper in her head and the hunt's true name under it.*

scenes.synopsis: Laurent's first word — the charm, the strain; the money, unoffered yet. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The drawing room, evening: pride's first offer — the de Varennes money, unoffered, in the French manner of offering money among ruins: by not offering it. Laurent has been ruined by paper before; the family knows this weather the way sailors know a sky. Pity would be the insult. The money stays where it is — pride keeps it, until it is needed.)*
> "Chérie." Laurent sets down his cup with the care of a man handling something loaded. "The offer is not made, chérie. You understand me." A pause. "Ruined by paper, the de Varennes, before. We know this weather. The money —" Another pause. "Stays. Until it is needed. Then —" He spreads his hands. "It is spent." — Laurent
> (T1 · look closer) *The fire burns low. The tea goes cold. The unspoken does most of the talking, as it always does in this room when the family gathers.* — remembered: *Cold tea going colder.*
> (T2 · tone) *"Unoffered, Laurent," she says, dry. "And understood. Pity is the insult, cousin — spare me that, at least. The rest is logistics."* — remembered: *Spare me the pity.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes the unoffered the way she takes all French money: as a fact, and as a loan against a day she hopes will not come. Pride keeps it. Need will spend it.* — remembered: *A loan against an unnamed day.*
> (T4 · stance) *She stands as his cousin — the family's weather acknowledged, its honor priced. She stands as the defendant — proud, and faced: no pity taken, none given.* — remembered: *Cousin and defendant both.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"The money stays unoffered, Laurent, and the pride is yours to keep. We know the weather, cousin — and when the money is needed, it will be spent."* — remembered: *Spent when needed, not before.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The cup, set down with care. The hands, spread wide. The money, staying where it is — in the de Varennes accounts, in the French manner, unoffered and understood.* — remembered: *Hands spread over nothing offered.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She answers his ruin without naming it, the way French families do everything that matters. The evening keeps its drawing room. The pride keeps its offer unmade.* — remembered: *Ruin, answered the French way.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the pride: unoffered, unspent, unasked. The money waits in France for a day she intends never to name.* — remembered: *The pride stays kept.*
> *(She keeps the pride. The drawing room releases them with the offer unmade — the money unoffered, the pity refused, the weather acknowledged, the need unnamed. The evening turns with the first offer unspoken — and the pride, kept.)*
> *He pours the dregs of the pot into his own cup and drinks them, and she lets him.*

scenes.synopsis: Henry's first word — the uniform, the man; the commission, unmentioned. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The grounds, morning: honor's attention — Henry's commission, offered in advance, the Horse Guards' name laid at her feet. On horseback, the way brothers do these things: at a walk, the reins loose, the offer made sideways. His worry, spoken plain: if his name taints her case. The commission waits — held, unspent, unasked. That is the point of it.)*
> "Rose." Henry shortens his reins. "The commission —" At a walk, the words come sideways. "Is yours before you ask it, do you understand? If my name —" The soldier's jaw sets. "If the Horse Guards' name taints your case, then it is spent. In advance." — Henry
> (T1 · look closer) *The morning takes them along the ride at a walk, the horses' breath smoking in the cold, the offer made the way soldiers make offers: sideways, and before the asking.* — remembered: *Offers made sideways.*
> (T2 · tone) *"The taint is priced, Henry," she says, dry. "And refused. Held, brother — the unspent, the unasked. Your name is my armor, Henry — and armor is worn, not spent."* — remembered: *Armor stays on the body.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes the commission the way she takes all Henry's offers: as armor, and as a debt she intends never to call in. Held, unspent, unasked — that is the point of it.* — remembered: *A debt never called in.*
> (T4 · stance) *She rides as his sister — the brother's name laid at her feet, the Horse Guards behind it. She rides as the defendant — the commission waiting, the taint feared and refused.* — remembered: *Sister and defendant both.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Keep your commission for the Horse Guards, Henry," she says, gathering her reins. "I will not spend your advancement on my claim. Ride for them — not for Hartwell."* — remembered: *His advancement is his own.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The reins, shortened. The jaw, set. The commission, offered before the asking — the soldier's way, which is also the brother's way.* — remembered: *Reins short, jaw set.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She answers his worry and refuses his name as currency, both in the same breath. The morning keeps its grounds. The honor keeps its offer.* — remembered: *Two things in one breath.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the commission: held, unspent, unasked. The Horse Guards' name stays in its scabbard — which is where names do their best work.* — remembered: *Best work, in the scabbard.*
> *(She chooses the held. The grounds release them with the commission offered in advance and refused in advance — Henry's name laid at her feet, the taint feared, the spending refused. The morning turns with honor's attention paid — and the unspent, kept.)*
> *At the stable yard he salutes her the way he salutes no civilian, and she is not sure whether to laugh or answer it.*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE TELLING (what to tell the household and the town: everything, the need-to-know, or nothing yet). The telling is decided; decide before the town tells it for her. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library, night: the telling weighed — the household, the town, the paper. The question is not what she knows but who knows it, and when. Rose walks the carpet's length and prices the three roads: everything, the need-to-know, nothing yet. The lamp burns low, and the night waits the way nights wait on decisions.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — The Telling:*
- **Everything** — *the open book, the whole house reading.* She tells them everything — the claim, the cousin, the paper — and trusts the household the way one trusts a locked room: completely, and at her own risk. (Consequence: no secrets to keep, no stories to contradict; but a house that knows everything tells everything, and the town listens at keyholes.)
- **The need-to-know** — *the measured word, the needers only.* She tells them what they need — the shape of the danger, not the shape of the paper — and keeps the rest where she keeps everything dangerous: filed. (Consequence: the household armed, the paper safe; but a half-told house fills the gaps itself, and its inventions are worse than the truth.)
- **Nothing yet** — *the silence, the held.* She tells them nothing — the claim is hers to carry until the paper is found — and the household goes on as before, which is the kindest lie she owns. (Consequence: no witness, no whisper, the hunt unobserved; but a house kept in the dark navigates by rumor, and rumor navigates badly.)
> *(The choice goes into the ledger, and with it the manner of the telling: the open book, the measured word, or the silence. The claim was always going to be known. The telling — the who, the when, the how much — is hers.)*
