scenes.prose:
> *(The morning calls, and the claim traveling with them. It arrives the way all town news arrives: sideways, in the middle of somebody else's sentence. Mrs. Almer says "your cousin" as if Rose had always had one. Miss Pratt asks after "the papers" with the sympathy of a woman enjoying herself enormously. By noon Letitia has the whole of it, hawk-precise: received, the cousin is; liked, the cousin is; and pitied — which is doing his work for him faster than any solicitor could.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The cards on the tray tell the week's story in the order they were left: the curious first, the kind second, and the ones who came only to look arriving last and staying longest. The claim travels faster than the post. The cousin's name rides ahead of him, liked before it is known.* — remembered: *The claim outruns the post.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She notes the order of it — received, liked, pitied — and prices the pity highest, the way one prices the weapon and not the wound. Let the town pity him. Pity is a debt, and debts can be collected.* — remembered: *Pity priced like a weapon.*
> (T3 · stance) *Defendant first this morning, campaigner second, woman third: the order the week requires. The drawing rooms are the claim's new address. She will learn every room's weather before Thursday.* — remembered: *Three orders for the week.*
> (T4 · tone) *Dry, for herself: "The town's tongue, then." Quiet, for the callers — she gives them nothing to carry home but good manners. Steady, for the week ahead. The murmur is weather; she dresses for weather.* — remembered: *Dressing for weather.*
> (T5 · look closer) *Letitia lays the pity down last, the way one lays the sharpest knife last on the table. "He pities you, darling. The town has decided to pity you through him." It is doing his work for him. She will do hers.* — remembered: *The town does his work.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *With the calls she is gracious — the morning made, the tea poured, the curiosity fed nothing but cake. With the murmur she is politely deaf. With herself she is the defendant, and keeping.* — remembered: *Cake for the curious.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *What the town tongues, the campaign uses. The claim's traveling is mapped; the pity's working is priced. Let it travel. Roads run both ways.* — remembered: *Let it travel.*
> (T8 · choice) *She chooses the coming: the week ahead, the drawing rooms, the campaign. The murmur is heard. The town is priced. What comes next, she meets standing.* — remembered: *Standing to meet it.*
> *(The calls end and the tray is cleared, and the murmur goes on without her the way weather does — the claim traveling, the cousin received and liked and pitied, the pity doing his work. She has heard it. That is the whole of the advantage, and it is enough.)*
> *The cards are stacked, the tray is cleared, and Rose goes up to change with the town's tongue still going in her ears.*

scenes.synopsis: the first coolness — an ally's honest waver; the fairness, allowed. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The afternoon call: a friend of years in the morning room, the ally's face familiar and the coolness new. She speaks of the cousin with the careful kindness of a woman who has decided to be fair, which is the town's kindest cruelty. The waver is honest. The honesty is what wounds.)*
> "Rose." Her friend's hands fold in her lap. "The cousin — Mr. Hartwell called, you know. He is —" A pause. "Respectable, Rose. And his papers —" The fairness, at cost. "One must be fair." — the friend
> (T1 · look closer) *The hands fold; the pauses come where the papers are mentioned. The fairness is entire, and it is the kindest cruelty in the town's whole repertoire — the cruelty of meaning it.* — remembered: *Kindness with teeth.*
> (T2 · tone) *Steady: "Fair, then. I have priced fairness before." Dry: "The kindest cruelty, and I know it well." Warm, for the years, because the years are the only part that matters.* — remembered: *Warm for the years only.*
> "His father poured money into the Park, Rose. One hears —" A look, away. "The debt is real, Rose. Even if the house —" She stops. "Forgive me." — the friend
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *The debt is real; the house is hers. Both things are true, and that is the whole difficulty — the difficulty she will carry into every room from now until the papers are read.* — remembered: *Both true, both carried.*
> (T4 · stance) *Friend first, defendant second: the order the years require. She will not make honesty pay for being honest. That is the one rule of the afternoon.* — remembered: *Honesty pays nothing today.*
> "Nothing to forgive. Be fair — it is the only honest thing to be." — Rose
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Be fair, and mean it. The honest thing is the only thing worth naming, and nothing needs forgiving because nothing has been done."* — remembered: *Fairness with intent.*
> "Whatever the papers say —" A pause, and the hands unfold. "The house knows its mistress, Rose." — the friend
> (T6 · look closer) *The hands unfold — the waver's remainder, the friendship's change. Whatever the papers say: the sentence hangs between them like a bridge neither will be the first to cross.* — remembered: *Neither crosses first.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She honors the years and prices the waver honestly: allowed, not punished. The call is kept. The afternoon is weathered, not lost.* — remembered: *The call survives the waver.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *The first coolness, faced and filed. The fairness, allowed. The friend, kept — remaindered, perhaps, but kept. A Hartwell does not bill her friends for their honesty.* — remembered: *A friend, remaindered but kept.*
> *(The call ends. The coolness has been faced, the fairness allowed, the honest waver priced and pocketed — and the house's knowing kept as the remainder, the change from the afternoon. Not a defection. A weather.)*
> *"Do come to the ball," Rose says at the door. "I shall need one person in the room who is fair on purpose."*

scenes.synopsis: Bell's office — the Gazette's independence stated early; the judge, entire. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The Gazette's office, morning: Mrs. Nance Bell among the presses — soft-voiced, sharp-eyed, mid-forties and entire, the paper's proprietor openly and the town's judge by habit. Rose comes with the claim's first week, and the terms are stated.)*
> "Miss Hartwell." Bell's voice is soft; the eyes are not. "The claim will be covered. Fully." A pause. "The paper judges. It does not take sides." — Bell
> (T1 · look closer) *The voice softens and the eyes sharpen — the proprietor practiced, the judge habitual. The pause is fully her own: covered, entire, without fear.* — remembered: *Soft voice, sharp eyes.*
> (T2 · tone) *Steady: "Fully. I have priced fully before." Dry: "The judge entire, proprietor — noted, and honored." Respectful, because the paper has earned it.* — remembered: *Respect for the unbuyable.*
> "The cousin's papers will be read. Your papers will be read." A look. "The verdict will be the paper's. Not yours. Not his." — Bell
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *Both sides read; neither side favored. That is the term, and it is the only term worth having — a judge who cannot be bought is the only judge whose verdict counts.* — remembered: *Neither side favored.*
> (T4 · stance) *Subject first, reader second: the order the office requires. She stands to be covered the way she stands to be read — openly, and without flinching.* — remembered: *Openly, without flinching.*
> "The paper's, Mrs. Bell. I would not have it otherwise — you know that." — Rose
> (T5 · dialogue) *"It was never otherwise, and never will be. The paper's verdict is the only one worth having, and we both know it."* — remembered: *Never otherwise.*
> "The war was covered fully. The claim will be covered fully." A nod. "Bell is unbuyable. Even by the woman the paper favors." — Bell
> (T6 · look closer) *The eyes soften a fraction — the war, remembered. The nod is the claim's: covered, fully. The pause after unbuyable is the whole of Bell's philosophy, and it does not blink.* — remembered: *She does not blink.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She honors the proprietor and prices the independence honestly: entire, and exactly what it costs. The office is left on the paper's terms, which are the only terms.* — remembered: *Left on the paper's terms.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *Bell judges and does not side; Bell covers fully; Bell is unbuyable even by the woman the paper favors. File it under the things that cannot be moved, and be glad.* — remembered: *Filed under immovable.*
> *(The office releases her. The terms are stated and entire — the claim covered fully, both sides' papers read, the verdict the paper's, Bell unbuyable. The presses run on. The independence holds the way good paper holds ink: completely.)*
> *The presses run, the terms hold, and Rose walks out with the unbuyable in her head like a coin she cannot spend and would not.*

scenes.synopsis: the season's flower — white lilies chosen; purity, the unassailable. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The flower room, morning: white lilies, ordered — the season's flower, purity itself. Not sentiment: strategy. A paper hunt dressed in flowers no one can criticize. The tall vases, the order given, the unassailable maintained stem by stem.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The order goes into the book in her own hand — white lilies, the tall vases, every room that matters. The flower room smells of stems and water.* — remembered: *In her own hand.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She chooses the lilies the way she chooses everything now: for what they say without speaking. Purity. The unassailable. Let the town read the flowers and find nothing to fault.* — remembered: *What they say unsaid.*
> (T3 · stance) *She stands as the housekeeper — the rooms dressed, the statement made. She stands as the defendant — the unassailable, arranged.* — remembered: *Dressed and unassailable.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet, to the empty flower room: "White, stem by stem." Dry: "Let them criticize the lilies. They will need the practice."* — remembered: *Let them practice.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The tall vases wait in their row, empty and expectant. By evening they will stand like sentries — white, blameless, and entirely on her side.* — remembered: *White sentries, expected by evening.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She instructs the gardener's boy with the gravity of a general issuing orders. He nods, solemn as a guardsman. The lilies will come.* — remembered: *Orders like a general.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the lilies: ordered, incoming, unassailable. The hunt's days will have their flowers, and the flowers will have nothing to answer for.* — remembered: *Flowers with clean records.*
> (T8 · choice) *The flower — the season's, and ordered. The house — dressed, and blameless. The morning — faced, and filed.* — remembered: *Blameless by evening.*
> *(She chooses the lilies. The flower room releases her with the order given — white, stem by stem, the tall vases waiting, the unassailable maintained. The chapter turns with the season's flower ordered — and the purity, kept.)*
> *On the way out she straightens one vase that needs no straightening, and the gardener's boy salutes her with the watering can.*

scenes.synopsis: Letitia's listening — the lawyers named, the cousin himself Thursday; the hawk's harvest. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room: Letitia with the week's best intelligence — the hawk's listening entire, the lawyers' name priced. The bonnet is shed; the eyes are bright with the pleasure of a harvest.)*
> "The firm, darling." Letitia's gloves come off. "Respectable — the cousin's men. And the cousin himself —" Her voice lowers. "Comes himself. Thursday." — Letitia
> (T1 · look closer) *The gloves come off and the voice lowers — the hawk's two weathers, business and gravity. Thursday. Himself. The counting is done; the coming is the news.* — remembered: *Thursday is the news.*
> (T2 · tone) *Sharp: "Himself, Aunt?" Dry: "Thursday, then. Noted, and faced." Steady, because the week requires it.* — remembered: *Steady for the week.*
> "Thirty. Respectable, courteous — a country gentleman." A pause. "And kind, darling." The gravity. "That is the danger. The kind." — Letitia
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *Kind is the danger. Noted, and filed where she files all Letitia's warnings: under gospel, and under weapons to be answered.* — remembered: *Danger wears kindness.*
> (T4 · stance) *Niece first, defendant second: the order the morning room requires. She stands dared by the news and braced for the Thursday, the way one stands for weather coming.* — remembered: *Braced for Thursday.*
> "Kind, Aunt. Then we will be kinder — and better papered." — Rose
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Kinder, and better papered — that is decided, and I vow it. Thursday, then. We will be ready to face it."* — remembered: *Vowed: kinder, better papered.*
> "The town says he pities you, darling." The hawk's edge, at last. "The pity —" A look. "Is his weapon. Worse than hatred." — Letitia
> (T6 · look closer) *The beam steadies into the edge — the hawk's two weathers again. The pity is his weapon, worse than hatred. Laid on the table last, like the sharpest knife.* — remembered: *Worse than hatred.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She honors the harvester with the morning's sweetest tea and the full honors of the listened-to. The hawk is fed; the intelligence is paid for in ceremony.* — remembered: *Ceremony as payment.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *The kind, filed as the danger. The pity, priced as the weapon. The Thursday, faced. The intelligence is kept; the aunt is kept; the week turns.* — remembered: *The week turns.*
> *(The morning room releases her with the harvest filed — the lawyers named and respectable, the cousin himself on Thursday, the pity his weapon and worse than hatred, the kind the danger. She walks out with the week's shape in her head like a map: the firm, the Thursday, the himself.)*
> *The bonnet lies shed, the gloves are off, and Rose climbs to dress with Thursday coming at her like weather.*

scenes.synopsis: the sponsors' first smell — money stirring at the City's edge; the forced sale, scented. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library, evening: Quill's report, the hawk's ears — money stirring at the City's edge, the sponsors' first smell. Moneyed men scenting a forced sale the way hounds scent weather. The claim is a week old. The money is already moving.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The report smells of money the way a kennel smells of hounds — the stirring, the scenting, the already-moving. Quill's men caught it; the hawk's ears confirmed it. A week old, the claim, and the hounds are out.* — remembered: *A kennel smell of money.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *The money moves; she notes where. A forced sale scented this early means the sponsors have priced her losing — which means the campaign must price them wrong, publicly.* — remembered: *Where the money moves.*
> (T3 · stance) *Defendant first, campaigner second, mistress third: the order the evening requires. The Park is the thing held; the money is the thing watched. She stands holding, and mapping.* — remembered: *Holding and mapping.*
> (T4 · tone) *Dry: "A week old, and the hounds already out." Quiet, for the report's edge. Sharp, for the scent — the money will learn that Hartwell Park is not carrion.* — remembered: *Not carrion.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The hounds are moneyed men, and moneyed men are patient the way hounds are patient: until the quarry moves. She will not move the way they expect.* — remembered: *She will not oblige them.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *With the report she is the evening's own — read, filed, used. With the money she is the watcher. With herself she is the defendant: kept, and keeping.* — remembered: *Three roles, one evening.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *The stirring, filed. The scented sale, noted. The week, turned. The sponsors have smelled; she has noted. The smelling is mutual now.* — remembered: *Smelled, and smelling back.*
> (T8 · choice) *She chooses the held: the house entire, the money faced, the week kept. The money stirs; the sale is scented; the house is held. That is the whole of the answer.* — remembered: *Held: the house.*
> *(The report is filed and the scent lingers — money stirring at the City's edge, the hounds out for a forced sale, the claim a week old. The evening holds the smelling the way evenings hold weather: noted, and priced. The house is held entire.)*
> *She blows the lamp out and sits in the dark a moment, listening to the house settle on its beams like an animal settling into sleep.*

scenes.synopsis: the night's reckoning — the claim priced without figures; the defendant's books. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library, night: the night's arithmetic done on the blotter's margin — the claim's shape, the posture chosen, the telling decided. No figures. The mortgages, the debt, the settlement all unnumbered, by discipline. She does the reckoning the way she has learned to: once for the sum, once for the nerve. The sum is the house. The nerve is hers.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The blotter's margin holds the arithmetic in her own hand — the claim's shape, the posture chosen, the telling decided. No figures anywhere. The discipline holds the way good posture holds: without thinking.* — remembered: *Good posture, unthinking.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *Once for the sum, once for the nerve. The house is the sum. The nerve is hers. The unnumbered is not the unknown — it is the refused-to-be-priced.* — remembered: *Twice reckoned.*
> (T3 · stance) *Economist first, defendant second, Hartwell third: the order the night requires. The books balance without a single figure, because the figures are not the point. The point is the holding.* — remembered: *Figures are not the point.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet, to the empty library: "The sum is the house, blotter. The nerve is mine." Dry: "No figures. The discipline stands."* — remembered: *Addressing the blotter.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The margin fills and the lamp burns lower, and the arithmetic comes out the way it always comes out: the house, entire; the nerve, hers; the night, kept.* — remembered: *It always comes out the same.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *With the blotter she is the night's own — reckoning, filing, done. With the claim she is the defendant. With herself she is the keeper of the books that need no figures.* — remembered: *Keeper of figureless books.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *The sum, kept: the house. The nerve, kept: hers. The night, kept: the reckoned. The books balance. They always balance when the discipline holds.* — remembered: *Everything kept.*
> (T8 · choice) *She chooses the defended: the arithmetic honest, the night kept, the house the sum and the nerve hers. The season is the ninth, and it is defended.* — remembered: *The defense holds.*
> *(The margin holds the reckoning — the claim shaped, the posture chosen, the telling decided, no figures by discipline — and the night holds the arithmetic the way nights hold accounts: honestly. The sum is the house. The nerve is hers.)*
> *She lays the pen down, goes up the stairs two at a time the way she used to at twelve, and sleeps before the lamp is cold.*

scenes.synopsis: Augusta's night counsel — the pearls promised for the hearing; continuity, entire. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta's sitting room, night: the Dowager's night counsel — the claim's week reviewed, the defendant's posture weighed. The spectacles are off. The grandmother is on.)*
> "The week, child." Augusta considers the fire. "The letter, the cousin, the claim — well received. The posture —" A nod. "Chosen. Now." The grandmother's weight. "The pearls." — Augusta
> (T1 · look closer) *The fire is considered and the week reviewed — the well-received, the chosen. The nod is the posture's own: decided, and kept. The spectacles are off, which means this is the grandmother speaking, not the Dowager.* — remembered: *Spectacles off: the grandmother.*
> (T2 · tone) *Warm: "The pearls, Grandmama — are they promised?" Steady, for the night's counsel. Dry, because continuity deserves a little dryness: "I have priced continuity before."* — remembered: *Asking after the pearls.*
> "Promised. My mother's — Hartwell continuity made visible." A look. "For the hearing, child. When it comes." — Augusta
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *Promised, not worn. Not yet. The pearls wait for the hearing the way good soldiers wait for the order: ready, and still.* — remembered: *Waiting like good soldiers.*
> (T4 · stance) *Pupil first, granddaughter second, heir third: the order the sitting room requires. She stands counseled and receiving, the promised kept in trust until the wearing.* — remembered: *Pupil first tonight.*
> "Worn, Grandmama. When it comes — visible, entire." — Rose
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Visible, and entire — I vow it. The pearls will be kept till the hearing, and then they will be worn, and the town will see what continuity looks like."* — remembered: *Vowed: visible.*
> "And the cousin — thirty, respectable, kind." A tap of the finger. "Pity him back, child. It is the only answer to pity." — Augusta
> (T6 · look closer) *The spectacles return; the Dowager is back. The tap is the command's own: pity answered before it is asked. Augusta's counsel, entire — the only answer, priced and filed.* — remembered: *The Dowager returns.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She stands commanded like a soldier and honoring like a granddaughter, and answers like a Hartwell: the pity will be answered, back, in full.* — remembered: *Commanded like a soldier.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She curtsies — the sitting room's full stop, the night's. The pearls, promised and pocketed. The counsel, filed. Pity back: commanded, and vowed.* — remembered: *Curtsying out the night.*
> *(The sitting room releases her with the week reviewed — the posture weighed, the continuity priced, the pearls promised for the hearing — and the pity answered before it was asked. The grandmother's counsel, filed entire.)*
> *She kisses Augusta's cheek at the door — an extravagance, for them — and the Dowager pretends not to notice, which is the same as noticing.*

scenes.synopsis: the letter filed — the week's close; the kept, scheduled. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library, late: the letter filed — the week's close, the claim's paper put by with the posture chosen and the telling decided. The firm's seal, broken. The clerk's hand, read. The courtesy, noted as the weapon it is. Rose files it in the war room's drawer, beside the map with the cousin's name penciled in the margin.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The seal is broken and the clerk's hand is read, and the cousin's name waits in the map's margin, penciled and patient. The filing is the late's own business: the lettered, the done, the put-by.* — remembered: *Penciled and patient.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *The broken seal, filed. The courtesy, noted as the weapon it is. The cousin's name, margined. Everything in its drawer — that is what drawers are for.* — remembered: *Everything in its drawer.*
> (T3 · stance) *Keeper first, defendant second, woman third: the order the late requires. The week's end is the filing's hour, and she keeps the hour the way she keeps everything: completely.* — remembered: *Keeping the hour fully.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet, to the empty library: "Filed, drawer." Dry: "The week's weather, kept." Steady: the closed, the priced, the turned.* — remembered: *Two words to the drawer.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The hand is read — the clerk's, studied. The courtesy is the weapon — noted, and priced accordingly. The name is margined — the cousin's, waiting for Thursday.* — remembered: *Reading the enemy's clerk.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *With the drawer she is the war room's own. With the week she is the letter's keeper. With herself she is the filer of things, and the filed stay filed.* — remembered: *At home in the war room.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *The letter, drawered. The week, closed and priced. The night, kept entire. The kept is scheduled; the week is turned. Thursday comes next.* — remembered: *Scheduled: Thursday.*
> (T8 · choice) *She chooses the begun: the filed, the kept, the scheduled. The week is closed. The season is the ninth, and it is begun.* — remembered: *Begun, not finished.*
> *(The drawer closes — the letter filed, the seal broken, the courtesy noted as the weapon, the cousin's name penciled in the map's margin — and the late holds the filing the way the late holds everything: quietly, and as a promise. The week's weather, kept.)*
> *She pockets the key, and it is heavier than a key has any right to be.*

scenes.synopsis: the answer drafted — Quill's counsel; the claim, the answered-in-form. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Mr. Quill's chambers, morning: the paper's first shape — the hunt's first finding, laid on the blotter. Not the quarry — not yet — but the shape of the search: the predecessor's filing, the country named, the deed room or the vault. The solicitor lays it out the way he lays out everything: as a promise with a schedule.)*
> "The shape, Miss Hartwell." The solicitor's finger rests on the week's finding. "The paper's first, miss." The professional's pause. "The predecessor's filing, miss —" The gravity. "Not in chambers, miss. The country, miss." He looks up. "A deed room, miss. Or a vault, miss." — Mr. Quill
> (T1 · look closer) *The finding lies on the blotter — thin, but real: the first paper of the hunt, the search given its shape.* — remembered: *Thin, but real.*
> (T2 · tone) *"The country, Mr. Quill," she says, sharp. "The deed room or the vault, solicitor — the hunt follows the scent."* — remembered: *Sharp: the country.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes the shape the way she takes all Quill's findings: as a promise, and as a schedule. The country named. The filing waiting.* — remembered: *Promised and scheduled.*
> (T4 · stance) *She stands as the client — the hunt's commissioner, the paper's pursuer. She stands as the hunter — the scent followed, the country faced.* — remembered: *Two roles, one client.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Follow the scent, Mr. Quill, and name the country, solicitor. The filing is the thing to hunt."* — remembered: *Following the scent.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The finger lifts from the finding. The promise sits on the blotter between them, with its schedule.* — remembered: *Between them, on the blotter.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She thanks him with the gravity the professional deserves — the client's thanks, the hunter's nod. The chambers approve of business done properly.* — remembered: *Thanks with gravity.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the shape: the country named, the deed room or the vault, the filing waiting. The hunt has its ground.* — remembered: *The hunt has ground.*
> *(She keeps the shape. The chambers release her with the paper's first shape in hand — the country named, the filing waiting, the promise scheduled. The hunt has its ground.)*
> *Outside, she buys a penny bun from the corner cart and eats it walking, all the way down Chancery Lane, like a schoolgirl with a secret.*

scenes.synopsis: the trial wardrobe begun — Élise's discipline; the armor's first seam. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The atelier, afternoon: the trial wardrobe — the hearing's armor, begun. Élise pins the brown holland with the concentration of a woman building fortifications. The trial wardrobe begins the way all Élise's work begins: with pins, and certainty.)*
> "Miss." Élise looks up, the pins in her mouth. "The wardrobe, miss —" The pins shift. "Begins, miss. The hearing's, miss." A nod at the holland. "The armor, miss —" The warm certainty. "Stitch by stitch, miss." — Élise
> (T1 · look closer) *The brown holland takes its first shape on the stand — the trial wardrobe's beginning, the armor's first seam.* — remembered: *Holland taking shape.*
> (T2 · tone) *"Stitch by stitch, Élise," Rose says, warm. "The hearing will have its armor, modiste — and the archive will find nothing to criticize."* — remembered: *Warm: stitch by stitch.*
> "The criticized-nothing, miss." The pins come out. "The pearls, miss —" The honesty. "Will have their setting, miss." A look. "Promised, miss. Not worn, miss." — Élise
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *Promised, not worn — Élise's plain speaking at its plainest. The setting will be stitched. The hearing will have its pearls.* — remembered: *The plainest plain speaking.*
> (T4 · stance) *She stands as the patron — the armor's commissioner, the trial's dresser. She stands as the friend — the twenty-two honored, the certainty trusted.* — remembered: *Honoring the twenty-two.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"The setting is what was promised, Élise — stitch by stitch, modiste, as you vowed. This is armor, and the hearing is what it is for."* — remembered: *What the armor is for.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The pins go back in, the holland takes its shape, and the atelier holds its afternoon the way ateliers hold everything: in good light, and at work.* — remembered: *The atelier holds its afternoon.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She leaves the modiste to her fortifications with thanks and a squeezed hand. Élise nods around the pins — the warm certainty, undimmed.* — remembered: *Thanks, and a squeeze.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *The wardrobe stays with her: the brown holland pinned, the pearls' setting promised. The hearing's armor is building, stitch by stitch.* — remembered: *Pinned and promised.*
> *(She keeps the wardrobe. The atelier releases her with the trial begun — the brown holland pinned, the pearls' setting promised, the armor building stitch by stitch. The first seam is in.)*
> *The pins hold, the holland shapes, and Rose leaves the atelier thinking of armor: the trial, the setting, the stitching.*

scenes.synopsis: the Park from the gallery window — the threatened house; the held, entire. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The long gallery, evening: the Park from the window — the grounds dressed, the lake holding the last of the sky. Rose stands where she has stood for nine seasons and looks at what the claim says is not hers. The house looks back, unmoved.)*

> (T5 · look closer) *The returning road has a particular shine to it: pity him in kind — for his father's story, his righteousness, his lonely crusade. It would be honest. It would also be war.* — remembered: *That particular shine, noted well.*

scenes.synopsis: Julian's counsel — the mended gloves; pity's answer, the lover's way. (Turns: 8)

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE ANSWER (how to answer his pity: accept it, deflect it, or return it in kind). The ball is Thursday; decide before the ball decides for her. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library, evening: the question of the week come due — how does she answer his pity? The ball is Thursday, and the town will be watching the answer the way it watches hems. She prices the roads: the accepted — let his pity stand, take town sympathy where it falls, be the gracious defendant the pity requires; the deflected — refuse its frame entirely, make every exchange about the papers and the case, give pity nowhere to land; the returned — pity him in kind, for his father's story, his righteousness, his lonely crusade, the pity-me-back the Dowager never forbade. Each road answers the pity. Each seasons the week differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The Answer:*
- **Accept it** — *Gracious, and taken.* She lets his pity stand — the gracious defendant, town sympathy taken where it falls. (Consequence: the sympathy flows her way, warm and freely given — but pity accepted is pity confirmed, and the confirmed are already half-defeated.)
- **Deflect it** — *Frameless, and refused.* She refuses pity's frame — every exchange about the papers, the case, the substance; pity given nowhere to land. (Consequence: the campaign stays on paper, where she is strongest — but deflection reads as coldness, and the town punishes cold women.)
- **Return it in kind** — *The pity-me-back.* She pities him in kind — for his father's story, his righteousness, his lonely crusade. (Consequence: the weapon turns, and the town delights in the symmetry — but pity given is pity owned, and the owner can be called cruel.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the gracious, the deflecting, or the pitying-back. The pity was always going to be answered. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the pity's ritual — dress so pity has nowhere to land; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "The ball's night — the London ball where Hugh Hartwell is received, and believed. The dress code of the unpitied: severe propriety carried into the ballroom — the law's severity, the ballroom's polish, nothing to criticize, nothing to pity. Pity must find nowhere to land: no softness to catch it, no falter to feed it. Serious colors permitted; brilliance permitted only as armor. **Editorial criterion: unassailability.**"
>
> **A. The Unpitied** — the grey silk severe; the ballroom may look, but it shall not land. Motif: the Hartwell oak, restrained at cuff and hem — the continuity, embroidered. Thread: **silver** (the unassailable, edged) / **dove silk** (the severe, matched) / **ivory whitework** (the purity, lit). Colorway: pearl grey + ash + silver. Accessories: the notebook left behind tonight; the pencil, pocketed; grey kid gloves, plain; the white lilies, one stem.
> **B. The Brilliant** — the black silk shot with silver; the French answer, the outshining. Motif: brilliance, disciplined — the outshone, restrained. Thread: **silver** (the brilliance, edged) / **jet** (the discipline, lined) / **matching silk** (the black, exact). Colorway: black + silver + pearl grey. Accessories: the silver pin, small; grey kid gloves; the reticule, capacious; the white lilies, one stem.
> **C. The Severe** — the white muslin starched, over silver; the English answer, the boring-of-pity. Motif: plainness, entire — the virtue, unembroidered. Thread: **whitework** (the purity, stated) / **silver** (the unassailable, edged) / **matching silk** (the starched, exact). Colorway: white + silver + pearl grey. Accessories: the white ribbon; pearl drop earrings — not the grandmother's, kept for the hearing; white kid gloves; the white lilies, one stem.
>
> *(The dressing room, Thursday evening: the week of pity, the receiving line, the believed to be answered. She dresses the way Augusta commanded — so that pity has nowhere to land.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *The unpitied, the brilliant, or the severe: three roads into the ballroom, and the whole strategy of the week hangs on the choosing. She commits — the grey silk, the black shot with silver, or the starched white — and the direction is remembered for the ball. Hair severe, accessories restrained, the mirror to be consulted briefly and then left alone. **Direction.** The ball's night — the London ball where Hugh is received, and believed. Dress to be unassailable. **Editorial criterion.** Unassailability — every choice must answer the pity, not the ballroom.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the ball. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** pity's answer in silk — the grey severe, or the black shot with silver, or the starched white — whichever the ball chose, worn straight and without apology. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, exact:** close enough for the receiving line, plain enough for the corners. No rustle, no train — nothing for the pity to catch on. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** the polish of the evening carried to the wrist. Long sleeves, unadorned — the grammar of the ballroom. *5 coins.*
> *(The gown's line is set, the sleeves fall straight — and the dressing room holds its evening light while the maid pins the hem.)*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, high:** the serious line at the throat. The ballroom takes the high ground tonight, and so does she. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, coiled:** braided and coiled close, severe as a verdict. Not a curl escapes to soften the effect. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Reticule, packed:** the pencil goes in the pocket, the notebook stays behind. Tonight the ballroom gets the lady, not the ledger. *5 coins.*
> *(The hair is severe, the reticule restrained — and the evening leans in through the window, the ball waiting downstairs.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, plain:** grey kid, pulled on without ceremony. The ballroom will be handled, not displayed. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Slippers, quiet:** soft soles for the receiving line. The unpitied arrive unheard. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Shawl, none:** no softness at the shoulders, nothing draped for pity to catch. The evening air will have to do. *5 coins.*
> *(Quiet slippers, bare shoulders — the pity looks for softness and finds the architecture instead.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Jewel, small:** the silver pin, plain and unshowy. One small seriousness at the throat, and no more. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** no perfume tonight. The ballroom will smell the lilies, not the lady. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, straight:** spine straight as a ruled line. The ball is defended by its mistress, and the mistress stands like one. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine straightens — the architecture of the unpitied — and the mirror is consulted briefly from the corner of her eye.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, level:** eye to eye with the receiving line. No downcast lids, no lifted chin — the level gaze of a woman with nothing to hide and nothing to beg. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, even:** measured, unhurried, kind. The pity will not be answered aloud — it will simply find no purchase in the tone. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, still:** folded, resting, unhurried. Still hands have never once betrayed a Hartwell. *5 coins.*
> *(Level gaze, even voice, still hands — the instruments tuned, the grammar of the ballroom spoken fluently.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, measured:** unhurried across the floor. The evening is worked at walking pace; haste is the tell of pity. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, rare:** given sparingly, and therefore worth having. A rare smile is armor the pity cannot price. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Nod, once:** one nod for the pity, priced and taken. A single acknowledgment, and then the evening moves on. *5 coins.*
> *(The step measured, the smile rare, the nod given once — the grammar of the ballroom, and she is fluent.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Turn, away:** when the dance ends, turn away cleanly. No lingering where the pity gathers. The turn is remembered. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — Door, held:** hold the door for no one and need no one to hold it. Answered, dressed, unpitied — the last pin of the evening. *5 coins.*
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. The completed direction is remembered. Owned jewels may be added freely from the open shelf, never as a step. No Crown SKU touches the ritual.)*
> *(Story morsel: the brass-polisher's boy looks up as she passes, cloth never pausing. "The unpitied, ma'am," he says, and goes back to the brass. The liturgy of the house, kept without being taught.)*
> *(Story morsel: a card slipped under the door in Augusta's hand — "Nowhere to land, child." She pins it inside the wardrobe door, where it will be the last thing she sees.)*
> *(Story morsel: the ball column of the evening Gazette, read aloud over the pinning — Bell on season weather, dry and not unkind: "The town watches, miss. The paper watches the watching.")*
> *(The coda — the mirror)* *The mirror is consulted briefly, and it answers: severe propriety carried into the ballroom, the gown that refuses pity — and the evening has its armor for the believed. The dressing room releases her. The ball waits.*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE POSTURE (first social appearance posture: face the ton with him, avoid him, or outshine him). The ball is half-danced; decide before the second half decides for her. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The middle interval of the ballroom — the believed priced, the sides forming, the evening half-danced. The question the interval demands: what is her posture before the ton, with him in the room? She prices the roads: the with-him — face the ton at his side, the gracious pair, the civility of the claim made visible, pity answered by proximity; the avoidance — keep the room between them, the dignified distance, a defendant's reserve, pity starved of its tableau; the outshining — be the brilliance of the evening, the center of the ball, the pity drowned in admiration. Each road postures the evening. Each seasons the ton differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The Posture:*
- **Face the ton with him** — *Gracious, and near.* She stands at his side — the claim's civility made visible, the pity answered by nearness. (Consequence: the town admires the grace of it — but nearness reads as concession, and the conceded are already half-believed against.)
- **Avoid him** — *Dignified, and distant.* She keeps the room between them — the defendant's reserve, the pity starved of its tableau. (Consequence: the dignity holds entire, the tableau denied — but distance reads as fear, and the town scents fear like rain.)
- **Outshine him** — *Brilliant, and drowning.* She becomes the evening's center — the ball's brilliance, the pity drowned in admiration. (Consequence: the admiration lands entire, the pity drowned — but brilliance beside a pitying man reads as cruelty, and the town never forgives the cruel.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the gracious, the reserved, or the brilliant. The posture was always going to be taken. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE COURTING (who to court as ally: Augusta's old friends, the young matrons, or no one yet). The old families are divided; decide before the division hardens. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The late hour of the ballroom — the tally priced, the divided named in outline, one gone and unnamed, the naming still to come. The question the hour demands: who does she court as ally, now that the ton is taking sides? She prices the roads: the friends of the Dowager — Augusta's old friends, the great ladies of the old families, the weight of the establishment turned to her side; the young matrons — already hers, courted openly and made into a phalanx, the allegiance of the future claimed early; the no-one — no one yet, the solitary campaign, a defendant's dignity, whole, no debts of gratitude owed. Each road courts the ton. Each seasons the division differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — The Courting:*
- **Augusta's old friends** — *The establishment, turned.* She courts the Dowager's old friends — the great ladies, the old families' weight. (Consequence: the establishment's own gravity joins her — but old friends come with old prices, and the Dowager's debts become hers.)
- **The young matrons** — *The future, claimed.* She courts the young matrons openly — the phalanx formed, the future claimed early. (Consequence: the young stand with her entire — but the young have no weight yet, and the old families notice who she chose.)
- **No one yet** — *The solitary, dignified.* She courts no one — the solitary campaign, no debts of gratitude owed. (Consequence: the dignity holds, the defendant owing nothing — but solitude reads as pride, and the divided harden without her.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the establishment, the future, or the solitary. The courting was always going to be chosen. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: Bell's verdict on the pity's week — pity as currency; the judge, entire. (Turns: 1 — the reading)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning Gazette, read over chocolate. Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, in her own dry voice:)*
> *"The ball received Mr. Hartwell, and the town believed him, which in London is the same ceremony performed twice. Pity is the season's currency, and it is spent freely on both sides of the claim — on the gentleman for his father's money, and on the lady for being the obstacle. The Gazette notes the spending and withholds the verdict: pity argues nothing, and the paper will judge the papers, not the pity. That is what papers are for."*
> (T1 · stance) *She reads it twice. The first reading is satisfaction: Bell has priced the pity as currency and found the spending wanting — the fairness of it, entire. The second is the reckoning: the town spends pity freely on both sides, the verdict still withheld, and Bell has made the terms formidable — which is Bell's way of making them permanent. The lesson files itself: in London, the paper that judges the papers and not the pity is the only paper worth being judged by.* — remembered: *Lesson learned: the paper judges the papers, not the pity.*
scenes.sting: The ball received Mr. Hartwell, and the town believed him, which in London is the same ceremony performed twice. Thread: **silver** (edged, for continuity) / **matching silk** (charcoal, exact) / **jet** (lined, for seriousness). Colorway: charcoal + silver + jet. scenes.synopsis: Bell's verdict on the rival paper — the gutter, the judged; the truth's champion, the entire. (Turns: 1 — reading the column)
scenes.prose:
> *(The Gazette, next morning: Bell's column on the rival paper — the gutter weighed and judged. The proprietor's verdict does what it always does: judges both sides, and serves the truth.)*
>
> *"The rival sheet has had its week. It printed a theft and called it history; it named a name and called it news. The Gazette has seen the memorandum — a page, whole in the late Mr. Rackham's hand — and the memorandum tells a rescue where the gutter told a theft. The entail was broken, irregularly, to save the estate; the mortgages' money kept the Park standing and did not purchase it. These are paper's facts, not the town's. The gutter will print again tomorrow — cheap type is nothing if not industrious. But the town may consider: whose paper proved the otherwise? The judge has judged. The truth, as always, is the Gazette's only client."* — remembered: *Judge has judged.*
>
> *(She reads it once, and the reading is the whole sting — the rival sheet weighed, the memorandum's rescue told, the gutter's theft undone in print. Bell judges both sides and serves the truth. The fifth chapter turns with the verdict filed — and the paper's facts, proved.)*

> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the gracious, the wintry, or the declared. The turned were always going to be answered. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE COUNTER-PRINT STRATEGY (answer every blow, answer once well, or let silence do the work). The gutter sharpens; decide before the silence is read as confession. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library, Monday evening. The week's first question has come due with the dark. The rival sheet prints the escalation; the ton reads the duel over its breakfast; and silence, both her counselors warn, gets read as confession by everyone except the law. She paces the carpet's worn path and prices the three roads the way Augusta taught her: for what each costs, what each buys, and who pays. The hawk laid out the thorns at noon; the solicitor priced them by afternoon. The open fight wants answering; the single stroke wants perfection; the dignified silence wants nerve. Now the choosing is hers alone, and the night is the counsel's last chamber.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The Counter-Print Strategy:*
- **Answer every blow** — *the open duel.* She answers every blow — each printing met with its answer, the ink fought in the open, the duel on full display for the ton to read. (Consequence: the ton sees the fight, and the fight becomes the week's whole news — thrilling, and exhausting; but a duel needs two, and the gutter is delighted to oblige, daily, in cheap type.)
- **Answer once, well** — *the single stroke.* She answers once and well — one measured rebuttal, complete and final, and then silence, held like a closed door against the week's noise. (Consequence: the answer stands alone and the ton reads it whole — dignified, and final-seeming; but one answer is one target, and the gutter prints every morning regardless.)
- **Let silence do the work** — *the dignified refusal.* She lets silence do the work — nothing printed, nothing answered, the gutter starved of its duel, the case left to the paper that matters. (Consequence: the silence holds its dignity and the ton respects the unprinted — for a while; but silence reads as confession to everyone except lawyers, and the reading hardens daily.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the price paid for it: the open fight, the single stroke, or the dignified silence. The counselors priced the roads; the night witnessed the choosing. The ink was always going to be answered one way or another. The signature at the bottom is hers, whichever road.)*

scenes.synopsis: the week's details — three diegetic options for the printer's visit dress; no coin cost; remembered. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Fashion beat — the print's escalation, and the afternoon's errand to the printer. The armor's details for the trade: the ink's answer in small things, worn where the type is set. Three diegetic options; no coin cost; remembered as her chosen face for the printer's errand.)*

> - (T5) **The reticule, spare** — *The week's cards, the errand's list, nothing heavier. The printer's errand wants a light hand and a ready one.* — remembered: *She packed the reticule light.*

> *(She keeps the week's face. The chosen detail goes on — the shawl, the gloves, or the lilies — and the charcoal keeps its severity into the afternoon's errand. The week is answered in the particulars: a woman who dresses for the trade she means to master, and masters it.)*

scenes.synopsis: the printer's ritual — ink and armor; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "The print's escalation — the rival sheet sharpening its attack, the ton reading the duel. The dress code of the printer: ink-proof, severe, unquotable — the chambers' severity carried into the week, nothing the type can catch. Dark colors required; no softness the ink can spot. **Editorial criterion: impenetrability.**"
>
> **A. The Unquotable** — charcoal-grey silk, the week's own, never to be quoted in print. Motif: the sealed letter, held at the hem in embroidery — unopened, unquoted. Thread: **jet** (the uncaught, couched) / **matching silk** (charcoal, exact) / **steel grey** (the severe, lined). Colorway: charcoal + jet + steel grey. Accessories: the steel pin, plain; black kid gloves; the reticule, spare; the white lilies, one stem.
> **B. The Pressed** — ink-blue sarcenet, deep as a fresh impression, the week's color. Motif: the folded sheet, restrained at the cuff in embroidery — printed, folded, finished. Thread: **silver** (the week's, edged) / **matching silk** (ink-blue, exact) / **pearl grey** (the deep, lined). Colorway: ink-blue + silver + pearl grey. Accessories: the silver brooch, small; grey kid gloves; the Gazette, folded; the white lilies, one stem.
> **C. The Armored** — steel-grey merino, severe, the faced and the defended. Motif: the bound quire, restrained at the bodice in embroidery — gathered, bound, kept. Thread: **jet** (the faced, edged) / **matching silk** (steel-grey, exact) / **gold** (the severe, lined). Colorway: steel grey + jet + gold. Accessories: the jet brooch, small; black kid gloves; the reticule, capacious; the white lilies, one stem.
>
> *(The dressing room, the print's morning: the escalation's week — the sharpened, the dueled, the read. She dresses the way the week has dressed her: ink-proof, unquotable, armored.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: the unquotable, the pressed, or the armored — the week's thesis, remembered. The hair is dressed severe. The accessories are declared and restrained. The mirror will be consulted briefly. **Direction.** The print's escalation — the rival sheet sharpening, the ton reading the duel. Dress to be impenetrable. **Editorial criterion.** Impenetrability — every choice must answer the press, not the parlor.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the week. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** the printer's answer — the charcoal silk, the ink-blue sarcenet, or the steel-grey merino, whichever the week chose, worn impenetrable. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, exact:** no softness for the press; the week's line kept close, the uncaught never caught. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** the wrist covered for the week; the severe kept to the cuff. *5 coins.*
> *(The pins accumulate — the gown's line set, the season's sleeves — and the dressing room holds its morning light the way the library holds the duel: patiently.)*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, high:** the impenetrable takes the high line; the press gets the week's high neck, and nothing else. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, severe:** drawn back and kept; the week's hair, dressed for the press. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Reticule, chosen:** the spare or the capacious, whichever the week needs; the carried, the kept. *5 coins.*
> *(The hair is severe, the reticule chosen — and the week leans in, the press waiting.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, black kid:** for the handling of paper; rooms handled, not displayed, and proofs the same. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Boots, quiet:** for the week's stairs and floors; the parlor's floors, unheard. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Shawl, dark wool:** the morning's answer to the press's chill; the cold, answered. *5 coins.*
> *(Quiet boots and black gloves — the press asks for the severe, and she gives it.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, steel:** the week's small weight, worn plain; the unquoted, the unpriced. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** the week's discipline; the press smells impenetrable resolve, not perfume. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, straight:** the week faced by its mistress, spine first; the room commanded by its entrant. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine straightens, and the mirror is consulted briefly from the corner of her eye.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, direct:** met eye to eye, the column's line; the press's answer, returned. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, measured:** the week's instrument; the press carried quiet, the words weighed. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, steady:** the handling unfluttered; the impenetrable kept in the fingers. *5 coins.*
> *(Direct gaze, measured voice, steady hands — the week's instruments, tuned for the press.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, deliberate:** the week's tread; the press walked, not hurried. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, none:** the impenetrable rations its expression; the week's smile, unpriced and unspent. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Nod, brief:** the week's answer, taken and given; the priced nod, exact. *5 coins.*
> *(The step deliberate, the smile absent, the nod brief — the press's own grammar, spoken fluently.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Turn, toward:** the week's facing; the faced, remembered for the rooms. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — Door, entered:** the printer's door, faced and dressed; the impenetrable, complete. *5 coins.*
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. The completed direction is remembered. Owned jewels may be added freely from the open shelf, never as a step. No Crown SKU touches the ritual.)*
> *(Story morsel: Élise at the fitting, pins in her mouth: "The press's dress, miss, not the parlor's. The muslin never lies." The discipline, kept.)*
> *(Story morsel: the week's rival sheet, folded small on the dressing table — read once, then turned face-down. "The unquoted," Élise says, turning it over. "The type takes the soft ones first.")*
> *(Story morsel: a card slipped under the door in Augusta's hand — "Impenetrable, child." She pins it inside the wardrobe door, where she will see it last.)*
> *(Story morsel: the Gazette's morning edition, read aloud over the pinning — the judge's column, measured and fair. "The paper," Élise says. "The paper's own terms, and no one else's.")*
> *(The coda — the mirror)* *The mirror is consulted briefly, and answered: the printer's answer — severe, unquotable, ink and armor — and the week has its armor for the watching. The dressing room releases her. The press waits.*

scenes.synopsis: the ton's reading — the week's armor judged in drawing rooms, and the duel still wanting its answer. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room, Thursday afternoon. Letitia's gloves are already off — always the first signal that the news is substantial — and the rival sheet lies folded on the side table, read and judged. She has spent the morning listening, and the hawk's morning rounds are worth more than a week of columns.)*
> "Well." Letitia folds her hands with the air of a woman delivering a clean bill of health. "The ton has read the armor — the charcoal, the severity, the whole unquotable grammar of it — and the verdict is in. The gutter cannot catch you. It has tried all week, and you are simply not there to be caught." — Letitia
> (T1 · look closer) *Bad news gets folded into linen-precise squares; good news gets waved flat. The sheet on the table is waved flat, and the bright eyes are doing the week's arithmetic early.* — remembered: *She received the reading and its verdict.*
> (T2 · tone) *Warm first — the report deserves warmth. Steady underneath. "Read, Aunt, and found impenetrable. That is the armor's whole grammar: there is nothing in it for the type to catch."* — remembered: *She showed the warmth and kept the steadiness.*
> "Nothing for the type. Exactly so." Letitia nods, brisk. "Pressed, impenetrable, armored — call it what you like, the effect is identical. The cheap ink slides off. But —" the hawk's eye sharpens — "the duel still wants its answer. The answer has either gone to the printer or it is being held, and the week is counting." — Letitia
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *The warning sits inside the praise: the dress has done its work, but a dress is not an answer. The pen's question is still open.* — remembered: *She took the warning with the praise.*
> (T4 · stance) *Niece first — the briefing is a kindness, and Letitia does not brief lightly. Campaigner second — the week's arithmetic still has an unanswered column. Hartwell third — the answer will be given when she chooses, not when the week asks.* — remembered: *She faced the week with the column unanswered.*
> "The armor is read, Aunt, and the ink is uncaught. That is the week's whole grammar, spoken aloud. The answer goes or holds on my timetable, not the ton's." — Rose
> (T5 · dialogue) *She says it plainly, with no performance. The hawk respects a plain answer more than a pretty one.* — remembered: *She vowed it plainly and kept it.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The gloves go back on — the report carried, the afternoon resumed. Letitia's eye rests on the folded sheet with the satisfaction of a woman who has read the duel and found her side holding.* — remembered: *She witnessed the holding and its satisfaction.*
> "Held, then, and well." The gloves button. "The duel waits on your answer, and the week can wait a little longer. The ton reads the dress, and the dress says: uncaught." — Letitia
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She pours — the cold cup has earned retirement — and takes the folded sheet with her to the library. Honors to the harvester: the hawk has read the ton so the ton need not be read twice.* — remembered: *She did the honoring and carried the sheet.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *Keep the verdict: impenetrable. Keep the price: the answer still owed. Keep the hawk.* — remembered: *She kept the hawk and the verdict.*
> *(The afternoon lets her go with the week's armor read and filed. The ton has done its reading — severe, unquotable, uncaught — and the only unread page left is the one she has not yet written.)*
> *The gloves are on, the sheet is folded, and Rose climbs to the library with the verdict warm in her pocket: the armor read, the ink uncaught.*

scenes.synopsis: the armor, worn — the week's dress kept through Thursday evening, and the duel's answer still unwritten. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library, Thursday evening. The charcoal silk hangs the way armor hangs at the end of a campaign day: honestly earned, briefly at rest. The ton has read it, found nothing quotable, and moved on to read the duel instead. The week's dress has done everything a dress can do.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The skirt holds its severity even off the shoulders. The lilies from the morning — one stem, white — stand in a glass on the dressing table, still pure. The armor, inspected, has no dents.* — remembered: *She inspected the wearing and found it sound.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *Keep the week's choice: severity was the right call. Keep the reading: impenetrable. Keep the quiet: the evening is owed.* — remembered: *She kept all three honestly.*
> (T3 · stance) *Woman first — the evening is hers before it is anyone else's. Campaigner second — the duel's answer still to give or withhold. Hartwell third — the house has worn severity before, and worn it well.* — remembered: *She took the stances and kept the evening.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet, because the library is listening and the day is spent. Dry. "Worn, library. The ton read the armor and found no purchase — and that, as they say in the cutting rooms, is the whole of it."* — remembered: *She set the tone and kept it quiet.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The strategy has been answered, the terms termed, the pen named or soon to be. The week has a shape now — ink-proofed, severe, holding.* — remembered: *She noted the shape and its holding.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She thanks the room the way one thanks a good second: silently, and with the books balanced. The candles are lit; the paper-knife lies where she left it.* — remembered: *She did the filing and thanked the room.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *Keep the worn: the dress did its office. Keep the read: the ton looked and found nothing to print. Keep the evening: it belongs to the woman, not the campaign.* — remembered: *She kept the dress, the reading, and the evening.*
> (T8 · choice) *The week asks nothing of the evening, and the evening returns the compliment. She chooses the keeping — of the dress, the reading, the quiet.* — remembered: *She chose the keeping and meant it.*

scenes.synopsis: Quill's tracing — the gutter's money followed home to the sponsors, and the claimant's purse found clean. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Mr. Quill's chambers, Friday morning. The rival sheet lies folded beside a ledger that has seen longer wars than this one. Quill's finger rests on a column of figures with the satisfaction of a man who has followed the money home.)*
> "Traced, miss." Quill taps the ledger once. "The money behind the gutter's type comes from the sponsors, not the claimant. Hugh Hartwell's purse is innocent of it. He has not paid for a single column, and I doubt he knows who has." — Mr. Quill
> (T1 · look closer) *The finger does not lift from the column. Fifty-eight years of paper have taught it where to rest. The figures are plain: subscriptions, donations, the sponsors' open purses.* — remembered: *She heard the tracing and its plain figures.*
> (T2 · tone) *Steady — the solicitor has handed her relief, and she takes it carefully. Dry. "The sponsors' money, Mr. Quill. A righteous man's unknowing purse — the ton's favorite kind of fiction, except this one is true."* — remembered: *She held her steadiness and priced the fiction.*
> "The purse is unknowing, miss, precisely so." Quill folds his hands. "The spending is the cutouts' — the last of them, spending the last of their paper on a righteous man's claim. Men like that do not advertise their ledgers. But money leaves tracks, even laundered money." — Mr. Quill
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes the comfort inside the precision: the claim's backers are spending what cannot be replaced. The gutter's purse has a bottom, and Quill has found it.* — remembered: *She took the comfort and marked the bottom.*
> (T4 · stance) *Client first — the advice is sound and the tracing is gold. Campaigner second — an exhaustible enemy is an outlastable one. Hartwell third — the claimant's innocence, noted and kept.* — remembered: *She filed the tracing and its gold.*
> "The cutouts spend, Mr. Quill, and the claimant never knows — a man with clean hands and dirty sponsors. What does the tracing name, and how long can they keep it up?" — Rose
> (T5 · dialogue) *She asks it directly, with the costs on the table. Quill has never needed the question asked twice.* — remembered: *She asked and let him name it.*
> "Names, miss, and an ending." The nod is a single dip. "The paper is spent, not invested — men buying ink by the week, not the year. It is the last of it. The last can be outlasted." — Mr. Quill
> (T6 · look closer) *The ledger closes with a soft thud, like a verdict being shelved. The spending has a limit; the week does not, quite.* — remembered: *She marked the limit and the thud.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She thanks him without gushing — Quill mistrusts gushing the way he mistrusts unsigned paper. The chambers keep their counsel.* — remembered: *She did the honors and kept the counsel.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *Keep the traced: sponsors, not the claimant. Keep the unknowing: Hugh's purse is clean. Keep the exhaustible: the last of the paper spends fastest.* — remembered: *She kept the solicitor and the tracing.*
> *(The morning releases her with the week's best news filed: the gutter is fed by money that cannot last, the claimant's hands are clean, and the last of the cutouts' paper is spending itself against her week. Outlast it, and it is gone.)*
> *The ledger is shut. Rose walks home through Friday's noon crowd with the week's best news folded small: a clean-handed claimant, and a purse with a bottom.*

scenes.synopsis: Hugh's disavowal — the claimant renounces the rival sheet's methods in person, and the human is kept. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room, Friday afternoon. The butler announces Mr. Hugh Hartwell with the particular gravity reserved for callers who arrive uninvited and cannot be refused. He comes in bowing — exact, unhurried, thirty years old and carrying himself like the house he believes is his. The pity is there, as always. So is something else: discomfort, plainly worn.)*
> "Miss Hartwell." The bow is exact. "I have come about the rival sheet, and I would rather say it standing. The gutter's methods are not mine. I have told the sponsors so, to their faces, and I will tell you so to yours." — Hugh
> (T1 · look closer) *The discomfort is genuine — a respectable man caught standing next to a gutter he never ordered. The pity precedes him as always; the errand, for once, is not pity's.* — remembered: *She witnessed the disavowal and its genuineness.*
> (T2 · tone) *Steady — the man has come in person, and that costs him something. Dry. "The gutter disowned to its own face, Cousin. I did not expect the week to hand me that, and I know what it costs you."* — remembered: *She held her steadiness and priced the cost.*
> "I did not order it, and I will not use it." Hugh's voice is level, the distaste unhidden. "A claim argued in the gutter is a claim half-lost. I have asked the sponsors to withdraw their custom. What they do now is on their conscience, not mine." — Hugh
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She hears the honesty inside the formality: he means it, and it will cost him allies. A man who disavows his own artillery is either honorable or finished — Hugh may be both.* — remembered: *She took the meaning and its price.*
> (T4 · stance) *Cousin first — the courtesy is owed, and returned. Defendant second — the sheet is answered, in part, by the claimant himself. Hartwell third — the human is kept, whatever the claim.* — remembered: *She did the honoring and kept the human.*

scenes.synopsis: the assembly's ritual — a gown for a door that may not open; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "The Assembly's week — the patronesses deciding, the black ball whispered, the Wednesday evening that may not include. The dress code of the doors: serene, unassailable — the drawing rooms' severity carried into the week, nothing a closed door can catch. Pale colors required; no defiance the patronesses can spot. **Editorial criterion: unassailability.**"
>
> **A. The Unassailable** — the pearl-white sarcenet, the week's own, never to be faulted. Motif: the closed door, restrained at the bodice in embroidery — faced, and holding. Thread: **silver** (the untouched, couched) / **matching silk** (the pearl-white, exact) / **pearl grey** (the serene, lined). Colorway: pearl-white + silver + pearl grey. Accessories: the silver brooch, small; ivory kid gloves; the reticule, spare; the white lilies, one stem.
> **B. The Serene** — the ivory crepe, deep as still water. Motif: the open latch, restrained at the cuff in embroidery — earned, and keeping. Thread: **gold** (the week's, edged) / **matching silk** (the ivory, exact) / **pearl grey** (the deep, lined). Colorway: ivory + gold + pearl grey. Accessories: the gold brooch, small; ivory kid gloves; the card case, silver; the white lilies, one stem.
> **C. The Resolved** — the dove-grey silk, severe, the faced and the defended. Motif: the threshold, restrained at the hem in embroidery — kept, and keeping. Thread: **silver** (the faced, edged) / **matching silk** (the dove-grey, exact) / **jet** (the severe, lined). Colorway: dove grey + silver + jet. Accessories: the jet brooch, small; grey kid gloves; the reticule, spare; the white lilies, one stem.
>
> *(The dressing room, the doors' morning: Almack's week in its three moods — whispered about, decided, faced. She dresses the way the week has dressed her: for a door that may not open — serene, unassailable.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: the unassailable, the serene, or the resolved — the week's thesis, remembered. The hair is dressed smooth. The accessories are declared and restrained. The mirror will be consulted briefly. **Direction.** The Assembly's week — the patronesses deciding, the black ball whispered, the Wednesday evening that may not include. Dress for a door that may not open. **Editorial criterion.** Unassailability — every choice must answer the doors, not the duel.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the week. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** the door's answer — the pearl-white sarcenet, or the ivory crepe, or the dove-grey silk — whichever the week chose, worn without a fault. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, exact:** no softness for the patronesses; the week's line kept close, nothing for them to catch. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** the wrist covered for the week; the serene kept to the cuff. *5 coins.*
> *(The pins accumulate — the gown's line set, the week's sleeves — and the dressing room holds its morning light the way the library holds a week's counsel: patiently.)*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, modest:** the modest line for the patronesses; the week's high neck, and nothing else given. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, smooth:** drawn back and kept; the week's hair, dressed for the doors. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Reticule, chosen:** the spare or the card case, whichever the week needs; carried and kept both. *5 coins.*
> *(The hair is smooth, the reticule chosen — and the week leans in, the doors waiting.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, ivory kid:** for the handling of doors; rooms handled, not displayed, and cards the same. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Slippers, quiet:** for the week's stairs and floors; the parlor's floors, unheard. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Shawl, pale:** the morning's answer to the doors' chill; the cold, answered. *5 coins.*
> *(Quiet slippers, ivory gloves — the doors ask for the serene, and she gives it.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, silver:** the week's small weight, worn plain — unspotted and unpriced. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** the week's discipline; the patronesses smell resolve, not perfume. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, easy:** the week faced by its mistress, spine first; the room commanded by its entrant. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine straightens, and the mirror is consulted briefly from the corner of her eye.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, level:** met eye to eye, the patroness's line; the doors' answer, returned. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, low:** the week's instrument; the doors carried quiet, the words weighed. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, still:** the handling unfluttered; the serene kept in the fingers. *5 coins.*
> *(Level gaze, low voice, still hands — the serene's instruments, tuned for the week.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, unhurried:** the week's tread; the doors walked, not hurried. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, slight:** the serene rations its expression; the week's smile, unpriced and unspent. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Curtsy, practiced:** the week's answer, taken and given; the priced curtsy, exact. *5 coins.*
> *(The step unhurried, the smile slight, the curtsy practiced — the doors' own grammar, spoken fluently.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Turn, toward:** the week's facing, remembered for the rooms. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — Door, faced:** the assembly's door, faced and dressed; the serene, complete. *5 coins.*
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. The completed direction is remembered. Owned jewels may be added freely from the open shelf, never as a step. No Crown SKU touches the ritual.)*
> *(Story morsel: Élise at the fitting, the pins in her mouth: "Not the duel's gown. The doors' gown." The muslin never lies. The discipline holds.)*
> *(Story morsel: the week's card, unaddressed, on the dressing table — no voucher yet. "Unissued," Élise says, setting it down. "The doors decide." She leaves it unaddressed.)*
> *(Story morsel: a card slipped under the door, in Augusta's hand — "Unassailable." She pins it inside the wardrobe door, where she will see it last.)*
> *(Story morsel: the Gazette's morning edition, read aloud over the pinning — the judge's column on the doors, measured and even. "The paper keeps its own terms," Élise says.)*
> *(The coda — the mirror)* *The mirror is consulted briefly, and answered: the door's answer, the serene — a gown for a door that may not open — and the week has its armor for the watching. The dressing room releases her. The doors wait.*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — LEGAL POSTURE (fight, settle, or out-wait). Decide before the week decides for her. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room, after Quill. The claim lies on the desk, unread — she has decided to read it after she decides, not before. The seal is unbroken; the breaking of it can wait for the choosing. Three roads, and the law's menu in order: posture first. Augusta would read first and decide after. Augusta is not the one being sued. She prices them the way she prices everything: once for the sum, once for the nerve.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — Legal Posture:*
- **Fight** — *Fight it in the open.* The defense argued where the town can watch — Sloane at the table, Quill at his elbow, the evidence squared and the witnesses rehearsed, the whole proceeding conducted where the light is best. (Consequence: a public defense is an honest one, which is its strength and its cost — the Gazette will print every blow that lands, and some will land.)
- **Settle** — *Buy the claim off.* A sum named, a paper signed, the claimant's gloves disappearing down the corridor for the last time, the whole matter filed under finished. (Consequence: the house gets its quiet back, and quiet is a currency — but a settlement looks like an admission, and the town will read it however the town pleases.)
- **Out-wait** — *Let the paper ripen or rot.* No hurry, no headlines. The house goes about its week, the law goes about its slowness, and the claimant learns what waiting costs when the waiting is mutual. (Consequence: dignity costs nothing and buys time — but the claimant's paper keeps working while she waits, and patience is only a virtue when it wins.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the fighter, the settler, or the unrushed. The posture was always going to be chosen. The signature is hers, and the ink is dry.)*

Accessories: the silver pin, small; the fan, ivory; black kid gloves, long.
> **C. The Severe** — white starched over silver; plainness as the argument. Motif: plainness — the serious, unembroidered. Thread: **whitework** (the purity, stated) / **silver** (the severe, edged) / **matching silk** (the starched, exact). Colorway: white + silver + charcoal.
