> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, high:** the severe takes the high line; the respectable, unquestioned. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, coiled:** the braid coiled severe, the kept order; no ornament. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Reticule, packed:** the notebook, the pencil, and the pencil's spare behind the ear. *5 coins.*
> *(The hair is severe, the reticule even — and the week leans in, the dead waiting.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, plain:** the dead handled, not judged cruelly; plain kid, no buttons. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Boots, quiet:** the chambers' floor, the archive's — the unheard step. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Shawl, wool:** the morning's wind, answered in wool. *5 coins.*
> *(Quiet boots, plain gloves — the judging's houses ask for the unheard, and she gives it.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, small:** the silver knot, unshowy — the even's own, no more. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** the chambers smell of dust, not of the lady; no scent. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, straight:** the judge's spine; the dead honored by their judge. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine straightens — the judge's — and the mirror is consulted briefly from the corner of her eye.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, level:** the judged met eye to eye, at the dead's table. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, even:** the judging's voice — severe, mannered. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, still:** the reverent stillness; the dead cradled plain. *5 coins.*
> *(Level gaze, even voice, still hands — the judging's instruments, tuned for the honoring.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, measured:** the week's walk, the judging's — worked and steady. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, none:** the judged week's own — none, and priced accordingly. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Nod, once:** the dead's answer — once, and taken. *5 coins.*
> *(The step measured, the smile none, the nod once — the chambers' own grammar, spoken fluently.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Turn, away:** the chambers' turn; the judged, remembered. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — Door, held:** the judging faced, dressed; the honored's own hour. *5 coins.*
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. The completed direction is remembered. Owned jewels may be added freely from the open shelf, never as a step. No Crown SKU touches the ritual.)*
> *(Story morsel: the brass-polisher's boy, polishing as she passes: "The judging's elsewhere, ma'am. The honoring's here." The cloth never pauses. The liturgy, kept.)*
> *(Story morsel: a card slipped under the door, Augusta's hand — "Even, child. Not cruel." She pins it inside the wardrobe door, where she will see it last.)*
> *(Story morsel: the morning Gazette, read aloud over the pinning — Bell on the grandfather, even and unsparing. "The grandfather broke the law to save the house. The Gazette will print both. Bell is watching.")*
> *(The coda — the mirror)* *The mirror is consulted briefly, and answered: the judging's face, the dead's — severe propriety, the dead honored in the seams — and the week has its armor for the chambers' eyes. The dressing room releases her. The judging waits.*

Yesterday's terms are barely dry — the debt named as his father's keeping, owed handsomely, the house neither claimed nor bought — and now the cousin asks her to come and watch him be believed. Not cruelly. He means it kindly, which is worse. He wants her to see the men who believe him, the way a man wants a witness at a christening: proof the thing is real because someone watched it happen.)*
> *(She takes the card to the window and does the week's arithmetic in columns, the way she does everything. First column: sea air, days of it, the sponsors' decks, moneyed men at close quarters. Second: the money behind the smiles — not Hugh's, never Hugh's, but somebody's, and the somebody matters more than the smiles. Third: the cousin at his most believed, asking her to stand beside him while he is believed. The Park lies green beyond the glass, kept and standing; eighty miles south, the tide is turning for Brighton.)*

> "Brighton, darling." The gloves come off, finger by finger. "The sponsors are afloat —" she counts them on her fingers, "— and they are moneyed men, darling. The kind who smell a forced sale the way hounds smell a warm scent." She folds the last finger down. "And our cousin among them, darling. Believed, and believing. It is a very pretty combination until you remember what it costs."

> "The week's whole argument, darling. Hugh's money, Hugh's men, Hugh's week." Her voice drops, which is how you know it matters. "The town loves a respectable man with a sea behind him, darling. > "Closely, darling, and with the wind." She considers Rose the way a general considers weather. "Dress for it. The sea is a harder room than the ballroom. It has no corners to hide a motive in — or a hem."

> *(The morning room, afternoon, and Hugh Hartwell himself — not the lawyers, not a letter; the man. He sits the way he does everything: openly, hands still, courtesy exact. > "Miss Hartwell." He gives the week its name plainly. "Brighton — the sponsors' week, afloat. I have come to ask you to come." A pause, and he meets her eyes. "Not as the defendant, cousin. > "You want me there to see you believed."
> "I want you to see the believing." The correction is gentle. "Not the papers, cousin. The men. The sponsors are moneyed men, and they believe the claim. > "And the watching —" She taps the desk once. "Watch the money, child. The men are the claim's face. The money is the claim's hands." A pause, the rarest kind. "The pearls are promised for the hearing, child. Not worn. Promised. The approach is dressed for, not arrived at."
> "And your sentence on the week, Grandmama?"
> "The sea has no corners, child. Dress for the cornerless. Watch the hands, not the face." The spectacles rise; the interview is ending. > "And the lilies?"

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — WHETHER TO GO (sail with them, follow by land, or refuse Brighton). The roads priced; decide before the week decides for her. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at night, and the week's hour come. The sponsors afloat, the cousin's asking, the Dowager's leave, the lover's offering — all filed, all priced, all waiting on the one signature that matters. She walks the roads once more, the way she walked them in the evening, and they haven't changed: the sailing buys her an eye on the believed, at the price of the sponsors' ground; the land buys her dignity, at the price of distance; the refusing buys her London, at the price of the town's invention. The lamp burns low. The house is asleep. The deciding is hers, and it won't wait for morning.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — Whether to Go:*
- **Sail with them** — *aboard, eyes open.* She goes aboard — her own eye on the believed, the sponsors' strength seen rather than read of. (Consequence: she boards the sea's room and watches the believed close at hand; but the watched is also the watcher aboard, and the sponsors' decks are not her ground.)
- **Follow by land** — *ashore, and dignified.* She follows by road — the week's strength observed at a distance, the dignity of the unembarked kept. (Consequence: the distance is kept — the sponsors observed, the sea declined; but the week happens afloat, and the absent are priced by the present.)
- **Refuse Brighton** — *London, and ungracious.* She stays — the claim's week ungraced, the town reading the absence. (Consequence: the absence is stated — fear or contempt, whichever the town prefers; but the ungraced week is the unpriced week, and the shadow sails without her eye.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and how it was made: the sailor, the follower, or the refuser, the tone of the going or the staying. The week was always going to be afloat. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: Bell's terms — the Gazette's eye on Brighton; the case tried in print, the sponsors leaning in. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The Gazette's office in the morning. Mrs. Nance Bell at the proprietor's desk — mid-forties, soft-voiced, sharp-eyed as ever — the week's notes in front of her: the sails, the sponsors, the believed, the shadow's first shape. The presses run below — the paper's heartbeat. The question gets answered bluntly, once: does the paper follow Rose's week, or its own?)*
> "Miss Hartwell." She looks up. "Brighton. The Gazette follows." A pause, and the bluntness is total. "The sponsors will lean — the debt romantic, the house damned, whichever sells the week." A direct look. "It never works. Not on this paper. Not on this proprietor. The case is tried in print, Miss Hartwell. At sea or ashore."
> "The sponsors' strength is the week's whole argument, Mrs. Bell."
> "The paper will weigh the argument." A nod. "And the shadow —" the bluntness again, "— the week carries one, Miss Hartwell. The paper sees it." A pause. "The paper does not name what it cannot prove."
> "Then the sides are untaken. Even mine."
> "Untaken." The bluntness holds. "Even yours. Especially yours — the town watches the favorite hardest, and the sea watches harder." She picks up her pen. "The Gazette will print the week's story. The Gazette will print it true. That is the whole of the promise."

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — POSTURE TOWARD THE SPONSORS (warmth, watchfulness, or open dealing). The decks ahead; decide before the sponsors decide her. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The cabin at noon, and the decks ahead. The sponsors' strength afloat, the believed waiting, the Dowager's counsel in her pocket like a folded handkerchief: watch the money. She prices the postures the way she priced the roads — the warmth boards the week as the hostess, grace disarming, at the price of being read as agreement; the watchfulness boards as the watcher, hands observed, at the price of the watched resenting the eye; the open dealing boards as the dealer, terms stated plainly at their own table, at the price of being priced in return. The noon holds. The decks wait. The posture is hers to choose.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — Posture Toward the Sponsors:*
- **Warmth** — *the hostess, welcomed in.* She meets them with her Hartwell grace whole — the sponsors welcomed, the believed's men honored. (Consequence: grace disarms — the moneyed men soften, the week warms; but warmth is read as agreement by anyone who wants it read so.)
- **Watchfulness** — *the watcher, eyes open.* She meets them as the watcher — the money's hands observed, the Dowager's counsel kept. (Consequence: the hands are seen — the money watched, the shadow priced; but the watcher is watched in turn, and people resent the eye.)
- **Open dealing** — *the dealer, plain-spoken.* She meets them with the claim's terms stated plainly — the keeping's debt named at their own table. (Consequence: the terms are stated — nothing hidden, the debt honored aloud; but the plainly stated is the plainly priced, and the sponsors price everything.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and how it was carried: the warm, the watchful, or the plain-dealing, the manner of the boarding. The decks were always going to be boarded. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sea's ritual — dress the defendant for the sponsors' week; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "The sponsors' week afloat — the moneyed, the watched, the men who lend boats to men who lend money. The dress code of the sea: severe respectability, salt-proof — the gown answers the deck, not the ballroom. Nothing to criticize, nothing the wind can pity. Serious colors only; salt is the gown's whole argument. **Editorial criterion: sea-worthiness.**"
>
> **A. The Salt** — sea-grey silk, plain and not sorry. Motif: the tide line at the waist, embroidered, kept low. Thread: **silver** (salt on silk) / **sea-grey silk** (tonal, plain) / **none** (no embroidery at all). Colorway: sea-grey + silver. Accessories: a borrowed telescope; notebook and pencil; plain sea-grey kid gloves.
> **B. The Tides** — deep blue wool, weathered on purpose. Motif: a coiled rope, unembroidered, at the shoulder. Thread: **steel** (deck fittings) / **blue wool** (tonal, weathered) / **matching wool** (plain, serviceable). Colorway: deep blue + steel. Accessories: an oilskin wrap; plain gloves; a small steel knot brooch.
> **C. The Mooring** — ivory damask, unassailable by design. Motif: the Hartwell oak, small, embroidered at the hem. Thread: **pearl** (high gloss, high risk) / **ivory silk** (tonal, exact) / **matching silk** (starched plain). Colorway: ivory + pearl. Accessories: an ivory ribbon; pearl drops she already owns; notebook and pencil; ivory kid gloves.
>
> *(The dressing room on the sailing morning. The sponsors' week: men with money, men with boats, men with opinions about both. She dresses the way she means to be read — severe, plain, impossible to pity. The salt will take what it likes from the silk; that is salt's business, not hers.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *Salt, tides, or mooring. She picks the line she can stand in for a week without feeling the costume. The hair wind-proofed, the accessories borrowed or owned, the mirror consulted once and briefly. **Direction.** The sponsors' week afloat — the moneyed, the watched, the cornered. Dress for the deck, not the ballroom. **Editorial criterion.** Sea-worthiness — if it won't survive a wet rail, it stays in the wardrobe.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the sea. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never as a step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** sea-grey silk, deep blue wool, or ivory damask — whichever the direction committed. The salt will do what it likes with it; that is known and accepted. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, close:** no train on a gangway, no skirts for the wind to catch. She will walk, and walk unheard. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** wrist-length, the way serious people dress at sea. *5 coins.*
> *(The gown's line is set; the sleeves reach the wrist. Morning light comes through the porthole in one neat slab and lies on the floor. She leaves it where it is.)*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, high:** sea air takes the high neck. Nothing for the wind to discuss. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, braided tight:** one braid, coiled, pinned until it surrenders. No ornament — the wind is ornament enough. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Wrap, wool:** a shawl with weight in it, one that won't fly. She tests it by tossing an end. It drops. Good. *5 coins.*
> *(The hair is pinned into submission and the wrap has heft. The week may begin whenever the men have finished their breakfast.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, plain:** kid, no buttons, for holding rails rather than teacups. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Boots, deck:** flat-soled, sure on wet boards. Vanity ends at the ankle. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Hat, tied:** tied under the chin, no exceptions. Losing a hat at sea is a farce, and she declines the part. *5 coins.*
> *(Boots that grip, gloves that hold, a hat that stays. The mirror gets one look from the corner of her eye, the way she checks a ledger entry before the ink is quite dry.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, small:** the steel knot, if that was the direction — unshowy, the size of a fingernail, and that is the whole of it. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** the sea smells of salt, and so will she. Anything else would be arguing. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, braced:** knees loose, back straight. A deck punishes stiffness; she offers it none. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine braced, the mirror answered from the corner of the eye — long enough to confirm the woman is serious, not long enough to flirt.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, level:** the moneyed will be looked at straight. Telescopes work in both directions. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, even:** no shouting into the wind, no whispering either. Carried, even, dry. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, steady:** one hand for the rail, one for the pencil. Both employed. *5 coins.*
> *(Level gaze, even voice, a hand that doesn't shake on the rail. The horizon is the audience tonight; the horizon gets no opinions.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, sure:** the gangway walked without hesitation. A pause reads as fear; there will be no pause. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, measured:** pleasant, not warm. Warmth at sea is read as nerves. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Nod, once:** to each sponsor's greeting, once, no more. A nod is a coin; she spends carefully. *5 coins.*
> *(The step sure, the smile rationed, the nod spent once. That is the whole grammar of being a woman watched from other decks.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Turn, to windward:** she turns her face into the wind when the wind asks it. It is only good manners. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — Door, held:** she holds the cabin door herself. No footman, no fuss, no ceremony about it. *5 coins.*
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. The completed direction is remembered. Owned jewels may be added freely from the open shelf, never as a step. No Crown SKU touches the ritual.)*
> *(Story morsel: the steward's boy, coiling rope as she passes on deck. "Wind's up by noon, ma'am," he says, and never once looks at the dress. The coil never pauses. She decides she likes him.)*
> *(Story morsel: a card slipped under the cabin door, Letitia's hand — "Serious, my dear. Not severe." She pins it inside the wardrobe door, where she will see it last. Letitia has never been severe a day in her life.)*
> *(Story morsel: the Gazette at breakfast, read aloud over the pinning — Bell on the sponsors' week. "Money afloat spends like money ashore," Bell writes, "only wetter." The table laughs. Rose does not.)*
> *(The coda — the mirror)* *The mirror is consulted once, briefly, the way she checks a ledger before closing it. It gives her back exactly what she asked for: severe, plain, salt-proof. She turns from it. Beyond the porthole, the sponsors' flags are snapping hard in the wind.*

scenes.prose:
> *(The yacht's first deck in the morning, and the moneyed men — the sponsors afloat, the week's grammar spoken in the sea's own room. They're what Letitia promised: hounds, honest, the forced sale's scent warm in their nostrils, the sea air doing nothing to cool it. The eldest has the hands of a man who built his money himself, and the manners of one who never needed to apologize for it. The younger two wear their wealth the way the deck wears its varnish: brightly, and meant to be seen. They receive her with the courtesy the sea teaches even landsmen — direct, wind-clean, no corner to hide a motive in. Hugh introduces her around with the pride of the believed, and among the manners, the shadow's first brush: one sponsor's man of business, below the rail's easy talk, too careful with a ledger — turning pages the way men turn cards they don't want read. The money moves through the claim's shadow the way water moves under a hull: felt, not seen. Hugh never sees the ledger. He never does.)*
> "Miss Hartwell." The eldest sponsor bows — unpracticed, honest in it. "The claim's face, eh? Your cousin talks of the house the way my father talked of his ships." The sea is in the pause. "Ships and houses, miss. They both want keeping."
> "They do," she says. "And both want honest hands on the ropes."
> "Honest hands." He laughs, a hound's laugh, no malice in it. "You'll find no others aboard, miss. Ask the ledger-man below if you doubt it — he'll show you figures till the tide turns."

> *(The rail at sunset, Hugh at his most believed — the sea behind him, the courtesy open as the light. He loves the house the way other men love scripture; she's seen it in his face since the asking. The sponsors' week is his strength, and the strength is honest, and he is honest — and the money behind the smiles isn't his to know. He never learns it. That's the week's mercy, and its cruelty.)*
> "Miss Hartwell." The sea is behind him. "The rail at sunset, cousin. The house is like this." A pause. "The standing. The kept." The rarest stillness. "My father saw it once, cousin. From the road. He never went in." A look. "I will go in, Miss Hartwell. That is the whole of the claim."
> "The keeping was his, Mr. Hartwell. The debt is named — his father's keeping, owed handsomely."
> "I do not hate the rebuilt, cousin." The pity holds. "I pity the rebuilding's cost. The cost is the living's, cousin — not the keeping's." A breath. "That is the pity. That is the whole of it."
> "And the sponsors' money, cousin — whose is it, behind the smiles?"
> "The sponsors are good men. Moneyed men." The honesty is total. "I do not ask whose money stands behind the smiles, cousin." A pause. "A righteous claim should not need to ask."

scenes.synopsis: Octavia's counsel — the evening's seeing; an unperforming hour at sea. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The deck in the evening, Octavia at the rail — thirty-four, the wind in her uncombed hair, the sponsors' week behind her and the sea's evening before her. The painter's counsel comes the way it always comes: plainly, and from the seeing.)*
> "Rose." The wind takes the words and gives them back. "The cousin is the most human thing afloat. The pity —" a look, "— the pity is real. That is what makes him dangerous. Not the papers. The pity."
> "And the shadow, Octavia?"
> "The week carries one." The precision is total. "I paint faces, Rose, and the money's face is not among the sponsors'. The money has another face. I have not seen it." A pause. "I have seen its absence."
> "Watch the hands, then. Not the face."
> "The sponsors are the claim's face — the money is the claim's hands, and the hands are not the sponsors'." A nod, once. "And the cousin —" the softness, rare in her, "— the cousin never knows. Keep him the never-knowing, Rose. It is the week's only mercy."

> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *The pity's danger filed, the money's absent face priced, the evening's steadiness held — the counsel taken whole.* — remembered: *the absence taken.*

> (T5 · dialogue) *"The absence, Octavia — worth the watching?" "The mercy, painter — the never-knowing kept?"* — remembered: *the asking done.*

The sponsors' week is ended; the return is tasked; the hearing is called. The debt is named the keeping's — owed, and handsomely. The house is named the living's, not the debt's.)*
> "The terms, Miss Hartwell." The solicitor's finger rests on the paper. "The debt — the keeping's, miss. Owed handsomely." A look. "The house — the living's, miss. Not the debt's." The finger taps. "The naming is the distinction, miss. The hearing is called."
> (T1 · look closer) *The finger rests on the paper the way the law rests on the facts. A professional pause; the tap that marks the distinction. Rose takes the terms the way she takes all of Quill's arithmetic: in writing.* — remembered: *she hears the terms.*
> (T2 · tone) *Steady: "The terms, Mr. Quill." Dry: "The hearing called, solicitor." Grave — the naming is grave.* — remembered: *she holds steady.*
> "The hearing wants what's proved, miss. The naming proves the debt." The finger travels down the page. "The not proves itself." A look. "The pearls — promised, miss. Not worn. The approach — dressed, miss. Not arrived at."
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She follows the traveling finger and takes the promised pearls — not worn. She takes the called hearing: filed. She holds steady amid the chambers' paper walls and quiet.* — remembered: *she takes it in.*
> (T4 · stance) *She takes the terms as a client takes a briefing, faces the debt as the payer must, and holds the house for the living, as a Hartwell must.* — remembered: *she begins the facing.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"What's proved, Mr. Quill — the naming?" "The hearing called — when, solicitor?" "The approach — dressed, but not arrived at?"* — remembered: *she faces it.*
> "Faced, Mr. Quill — the terms, the hearing, the called. The debt is the keeping's, owed handsomely. The house is the living's, not the debt's. The naming proves it."
> (T6 · look closer) *His professional gravity. The finger taps the distinction once more: the approach dressed, the pearls waiting.* — remembered: *she notes the calling.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She thanks him as a client thanks counsel — for the hour, and the man — and faces the debt as the payer must.* — remembered: *she thanks him.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the terms: the hearing called, filed. The named: the keeping's debt, owed. The rest: the house belongs to the living. The chambers, papered and turned toward the hearing.* — remembered: *she keeps her solicitor.*
> *(She keeps the solicitor. The chambers release her with the distinction drawn: the debt is the keeping's to owe, and owed handsomely; the house is the living's, and never the debt's. The approach: the pearls promised, not worn; dressed, not yet arrived.)*
> *And Rose walks out with the call in her head — the debt, the house, and what the naming will prove. Behind her, the paper-knife rests and the terms lie closed.*

scenes.synopsis: the return's ritual — one direction, twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, a reveal coda at the mirror. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "The last ordinary week before the hearing: the paper trail closed, the sponsors' week behind her, the hearing's date in ink. The dress code of the approach: severe propriety — nothing to criticize, nothing to pity. Serious colors; the gown must argue nothing and prove everything. **Editorial criterion: approach-dressing.**"
>
> **A. The Approaching** — charcoal silk, severe; the law's restrained line embroidered at the waist. Motif: the law's line, restrained at the waist — severity embroidered. Thread: **silver** / **charcoal silk** / **none**. Colorway: charcoal + silver. Accessories: the terms, folded; the notebook, the pencil; charcoal kid gloves, plain.
> **B. The Armed** — iron-grey wool, worked; plain and unembroidered, the week's price paid in cloth. Motif: the worked unembroidered — plain work, nothing to show. Thread: **steel** / **iron-grey wool** / **matching wool**. Colorway: iron-grey + steel. Accessories: the reticule, capacious; the gloves, plain; a small steel knot brooch, unshowy.
> **C. The Defendant** — deep claret silk, handsome; the Hartwell oak restrained at the hem, unassailable. Motif: the Hartwell oak, restrained — the standing embroidered. Thread: **gold** / **claret silk** / **matching silk**. Colorway: claret + gold. Accessories: the claret ribbon; gold drop earrings, owned; the notebook, the pencil; claret kid gloves.
>
> *(The dressing room, the morning after the return from Brighton. She dresses the way the Dowager ordered: for the approach, not the arrival. The chambers are not a ballroom, and men who read ledgers must be given nothing to read but the dress.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: the approaching, the armed, or the defendant. The hair severe, the accessories kept, the mirror consulted briefly. **Direction.** Dress to honor the approach without the arrival — the hearing's eyes, not the town's. **Editorial criterion.** Approach-dressing.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the return. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never as a step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** the charcoal silk severe, the iron-grey wool worked, or the deep claret silk handsome — whichever the direction chose; the dress decided, the body in it. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, severe:** no rustle for the chambers, no train on the hearing's floor; the approach walks unheard. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** her habit for business — to the wrist, as always. *5 coins.*
> *(The gown's line is set, the sleeves right. From the street below comes the morning's noise — a cart, a crossing-sweeper's broom — and the dressing room pays it no attention.)*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, high:** the respectable, unquestioned; no counsel's argument begins at a neckline. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, coiled severe:** the braid coiled and pinned, no ornament; the one vanity allowed is speed. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Terms, folded:** Quill's terms, folded once, into the reticule — the whole of her arithmetic, where her hand can find it. *5 coins.*
> *(The hair severe, the terms kept. Across town, the law is already at its desk; she will not keep it waiting long.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, plain:** plain kid, no buttons; she is walking into the chambers, not claiming them. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Boots, quiet:** quiet soles; the chambers' floor is not for announcing oneself. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Shawl, wool:** wool for the walk to the carriage — the morning street answers to no one. *5 coins.*
> *(Quiet boots, plain gloves — houses of law like to be addressed in a low voice, and she will oblige them.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, small:** the steel knot, unshowy; one thing, and small enough to miss. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** none — the chambers smell of dust, and she will not add to it. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, straight:** the spine straightened against the wardrobe; the mirror to be consulted briefly. *5 coins.*
> *(She catches her own eye in the glass — startled, for half a second, by how like the Dowager she looks this morning — and looks away first.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, level:** eye to eye at the law's table; she has never dropped hers yet. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, even:** even and unhurried — the voice she uses on bad-tempered mares and bishops. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, still:** still in the lap, or holding the terms; nothing fidgeted. *5 coins.*
> *(Level gaze, even voice, still hands — the approach's instruments, tuned and ready.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, measured:** measured on the stairs, at the door, to the carriage; the approach keeps its own time. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, none:** none this week; the approach is not a smiling matter. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Nod, once:** once, when the answer is made — once is final. *5 coins.*
> *(The step measured, the smile none, the nod once — the chambers' own grammar, spoken fluently.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Turn, away:** the turn from the wardrobe to the door; the room behind her, dismissed. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — Door, held:** the door held, the threshold crossed; the approach begins. *5 coins.*
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. The completed direction is remembered. Owned jewels may be added freely from the open shelf, never as a step. No Crown SKU touches the ritual.)*
> *(Story morsel: the housemaid, shaking out the counterpane: "They'll have you in and out of those chambers all week, ma'am." "Then I shall dress as if I lived there," says Rose.)*
> *(Story morsel: a card slipped under the door, Augusta's hand — "Severe, child. Not hard." She pins it inside the wardrobe door, where she will see it last.)*
> *(Story morsel: the morning Gazette, read aloud over the pinning — Bell on the week, short and unsparing: "The heiress has come back from the coast with her arithmetic done. The Gazette congratulates her, and remains unconvinced.")*
> *(The coda — the mirror) She turns once before the glass. The gown gives nothing away — that is its whole argument. She takes up the gloves, the reticule with the terms folded inside, and goes down to the carriage.*

scenes.synopsis: the last paper — the Network's last cutouts have spent their final pages on the righteous man's claim; Rose sits alone at the lamp and reckons it as texture, not revelation. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at night: the last paper. The Network's last cutouts have spent their remaining pages on the righteous man's claim — the sponsors' week, the believed, the shadow. The pages are spent; the paper is exhausted. She reckons it the way the night reckons: as texture, not revelation. The cutouts are never named. The unmasking is never here.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The night's arithmetic first. The remaining paper: spent. The cutouts' quiet work: done. The season's own sum: the last paper on the last claim. She reckons it by lamplight.* — remembered: *the last paper, spent.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She reckons the spent and files it. She reckons the exhausted and closes the file. She reckons the texture and keeps it — no revelation, just the week's work.* — remembered: *the reckoning, honest.*
> (T3 · stance) *Heiress, watcher, woman: she does the sums at the lamp, watches the money go out like a tide, and sits alone in the night with the pen.* — remembered: *the sums, begun.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet, the library's night. Dry, under her breath, to the empty shelves: "Arithmetic, lamp. The season's." Steady, facing the texture.* — remembered: *the dryness, filed.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The quiet belongs to the cutouts: worked, and withdrawing. The naming never happens here — not tonight, not now. The texture is the week's: the trial closed, the paper gone.* — remembered: *the quiet, noted.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *With the night, she uses the library well — the lamp, the quiet, the hour. With the last paper, she files the spent. With herself, she adds the reckoned to the week's price.* — remembered: *the filing, done.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the spent and files it. She keeps the exhausted and closes it. She keeps the night, and turns the library toward the hearing.* — remembered: *the keeping, done.*
> (T8 · choice) *The last paper: spent. The texture: kept, not revealed. The week: turned, closed.* — remembered: *the closing, chosen.*
> *(She chooses the closing. The library keeps the night — the last paper spent, the cutouts' quiet work exhausted, the trial closed. Texture, not revelation; the never-named, the never-here.)*
> *The lamp stays lit. The paper stays spent.*

scenes.synopsis: the farewell — Hugh's grace at parting; transformed or ruined, the texture of the cousin who accepts it. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room in the afternoon: the farewell. Hugh Hartwell stands with the return before him — the sponsors' week ended, the hearing called, the living to be named — thirty, courtesy whole, pity held the way farewells hold things: openly. The season will name him transformed or ruined — the cousin who accepts grace or the man who cannot. The afternoon does not decide it. The afternoon only keeps the farewell.)*
> "Miss Hartwell." The attention unhurried. "The week's farewell, cousin. The sponsors'." The rarest stillness. "The hearing will name the living. I will hear the naming — all of it."
> (T1 · look closer) *He stands the afternoon the way he stands everything: openly. He pauses the way the week pauses; he looks toward the living-to-be-named. Rose takes the farewell the way she takes all of Hugh's hours: standing.* — remembered: *the farewell, received.*
> (T2 · tone) *Steady: "Farewell, Mr. Hartwell." Quiet, because the afternoon is quiet. Human, because the grace is human.* — remembered: *the steadiness, held.*
> "My father poured the keeping, cousin. Year by year." A look. "The keeping's debt is owed — handsomely." The stillness. "The house goes to the living. I have heard the naming — all of it."
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She hears the holding: grace, taken. She takes the poured: the keeping, filed. She takes the heard: the naming, priced. She holds the steadiness against the afternoon's light.* — remembered: *the hearing, taken.*
> (T4 · stance) *As the hostess, she honors the farewell. As the mirror, she shows him the believed. As the Hartwell, she holds the naming's hour.* — remembered: *the honoring, begun.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Your father's keeping, Mr. Hartwell?" "The naming, cousin — you heard it?" "The farewell, cousin — the week's last?"* — remembered: *the honoring, done.*
> "Honored, Mr. Hartwell. The keeping poured, the keeping's debt owed, the house for the living. The grace — kept."
> (T6 · look closer) *The sea's memory is in the room — the believed, the week afloat. The sponsors' strength was shown, not read of, and Hugh is glad she saw it.* — remembered: *the keeping, witnessed.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *With the cousin, she honors the farewell at its face value, which is high. With the grace, she keeps it. With the afternoon, she lets the light do what it does.* — remembered: *the honoring, done.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the farewell: the week's last, filed. She keeps the heard: the naming, priced. She keeps the grace: kept. She keeps the afternoon: the room's, turned.* — remembered: *the cousin, kept.*
> *(He bows — the exact bow — and takes his leave. At the door he pauses, not turning: "The keeping was my father's." Then he is gone, and the morning room keeps the shape of his courtesy.)*
> *The door closes on the bow. His father's keeping goes with him, unpriced and unasked.*

scenes.synopsis: the parting — the offers answered; the moneyed men's manners at the week's end. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room in the evening: the parting. The sponsors take their leave the way moneyed men take leave — largely, the week's strength honored, the carriages called in good order, the farewells made without hurry. The eldest clasps her hand the way his father must have clasped a shipwright's — the grip of a man who trusts what he can feel. The offers have been treated — whichever road the turn chose — and the quiet work is done: the last paper spent, the ledger closed. The youngest, at the door, turns back to say the house will stand, and means it the way his kind means things — as a fact, not a wish.)*
> "Miss Hartwell." The eldest bows at the door — practiced now, the week's worth of bows behind it. "The week's been the strength, miss. Your cousin's house —" a pause — "your cousin's house is in honest hands. His own." A look. "The money's only ever the money, miss. Remember that when the town talks."
> "I will," she says. "The town talks. The house stands."
> And he laughs, and takes his leave, and does not know how much of the week's money he never saw.
> (T1 · look closer) *The leave is taken largely — the moneyed manner, the parting's own. The offers answered, the manners kept. Rose watches the week's strength go out in good order.* — remembered: *the parting, witnessed.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes the honored: the hospitality, filed. She takes the treated: the offers, priced. She takes the done: the quiet work, noted.* — remembered: *the taking, done.*
> (T3 · stance) *As the hostess, she parts them graced. As the treater, she signs the week's signature. As the Hartwell, she stands the evening.* — remembered: *the parting, begun.*
> (T4 · tone) *Measured, the room's evening. Dry, under her breath: "The signature, room. The week's own." Steady, facing the parting.* — remembered: *the dryness, filed.*
> (T5 · look closer) *They take their leave the moneyed way: largely, with the manners. The spending is the last paper's: done. The closing is the ledger's: shut.* — remembered: *the closing, noted.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *With the evening, she uses the room well — the light going, the quiet coming. With the sponsors, she parts them honored. With the parting, she files it under the week's end.* — remembered: *the parting, done.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the treated: the offers, filed. She keeps the honest: the hounds, priced. She keeps the evening: the room's, turned toward the hearing.* — remembered: *the keeping, done.*
> (T8 · choice) *The parting: manned, eveninged. The offers: answered, signed. The week: ended, turned.* — remembered: *the ending, chosen.*
> *(She chooses the ending. The morning room keeps the evening — the sponsors parted largely, the eldest's practiced bow, the youngest's backward-turned promise, the offers answered, the quiet work done. The money's only ever the money. The town will talk. The house stands.)*
> *The carriages roll off in good order. The evening settles the way evenings settle after guests — the room larger, the air clearer. The week's signature dries on the seven days.*

scenes.synopsis: the Frenchman's week — the last of the de Varenne money, spent; the illusion's worth, the freer. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library in the evening: the Frenchman's week. The Comte Laurent de Varenne, thirty-one, with the week's spending behind him — the last of the de Varenne money taken into the defense's purse, the family's final illusion priced and named. The season of the claimant asked what he would risk. His answer was the money. The money is spent — handsomely, on the keeping's debt.)*
> "It was the last of it, you know." Laurent turns his empty glass. "The money and the illusion both."
> (T1 · look closer) *The glass turns in his hand — empty, the week's spending done. The illusion gets its price; the expense gets its worth. Rose takes the week the way she takes all of Laurent's accounts: in francs of feeling, converted at par.* — remembered: *the week, noted.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes the spent: the last of the money, filed. She takes the worth: the expense, priced. She takes the freer: the poorer, honored.* — remembered: *the taking, done.*
> (T3 · stance) *As the beloved, she honors the spent. As the payer, she faces the debt. As the woman, she meets the evening plainly.* — remembered: *the honoring, begun.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet, the library's evening. Dry, under her breath: "The expense, library. The worth." Steady, facing the spent.* — remembered: *the dryness, filed.*
> "And the worth, Laurent?"
> "The expense was the worth." A shrug, very French. "Poorer, Rose. And freer."
> (T5 · look closer) *The handsome part is the keeping's debt, paid. The expensive part is the illusion, priced. The worth is the expense — and the expense was handsome.* — remembered: *the handsomely, noted.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *With the evening, she uses the library well — the lamp, the quiet, the hour. With the money, she honors the last of it. With the lover, she keeps the freer.* — remembered: *the honoring, done.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the spent: the last of the money, filed. She keeps the worth: the expense, priced. She keeps the evening: the library's, turned toward the hearing.* — remembered: *the keeping, done.*
> (T8 · choice) *The money: the last, the spent. The illusion: the family's final, priced. The lover: the freer, the poorer.* — remembered: *the spending, chosen.*
> *(She chooses the spending. The library keeps the evening — the last of the de Varenne money spent handsomely on the keeping's debt, the family's final illusion priced and named, the man poorer and freer. The illusion was expensive; let it be worth the expense.)*
> *The glass is empty. The money is spent. Laurent smiles like a man whose accounts finally balance.*

scenes.synopsis: the return's face — the day's choices; three diegetic options; no coin cost; remembered. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Fashion beat — the return's day. The dressing room in the morning; the hearing's approach on the other side of the glass. She dresses the day the way the turn asks: the approach, priced and dressed. Three things to choose among for the day's face; no coin cost; the choice remembered.)*
> - (T1) **The charcoal silk, severe** — *The gown again — charcoal silk, severe. The approach's own face. London's eyes will find nothing to pity and nothing to criticize.* — remembered: *The severe, worn.*
> - (T2) **The claret silk, handsome** — *Deep claret, handsome: the payer's face, the keeping's color. The debt honored in the wearing of it.* — remembered: *The handsome, worn.*
> - (T3) **The lilies, worn** — *White lilies at the throat, worn not pressed: purity of intent, unassailable, the season's constant going with her into the watching.* — remembered: *The lilies, worn.*
> - (T4) **Choose** — *The choosing done — the day's face decided, the approach's dress taking shape.* — remembered: *The face, chosen.*
> - (T5) **The accessories, day's** — *The terms folded into the reticule; the notebook and the pencil beside them. The day travels equipped.* — remembered: *The day, equipped.*
> - (T6) **The hair, coiled severe** — *The braid coiled severe; no ornament. The approach's hair asks for nothing.* — remembered: *The severe, kept.*
> - (T7) **The mirror, consulted** — *One look, brief. The mirror shows the return's day back at her; she nods once and turns away.* — remembered: *The mirror, answered.*
> - (T8) **Remembered micro-decision** — *Keep the face chosen, the day priced, the week turned toward the hearing.* — remembered: *The day's face, kept.*
> *(She keeps the day's face. The chosen things go on — the approached, the priced, the dressed — and the terms go folded into the reticule, and the notebook goes with the pencil, and the hair goes up severe for the approach. The week's turn continues with the face chosen — defendant, payer, Hartwell, whichever she chose — it is the face of a woman dressing the hearing's approach in a London that watches.)*
> *The day is set, the face is worn, and London waits — and Rose dresses it.*

scenes.synopsis: the paper's week-end — the Gazette's terms; the verdict printed, the promise kept. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The Gazette's office in the afternoon: the paper's week-end. Mrs. Nance Bell, mid-forties, at the proprietor's desk with the week's edition — the believed, the moneyed, the shadow seen and unnamed. The Gazette prints the week's story on its own terms: the strength weighed, the shadow watched, the sides untaken. Bell judges; Bell never takes sides. That is what makes the paper worth keeping.)*
> "Miss Hartwell." The proprietor looks up. "The week-end. The Gazette prints." A pause. "The sponsors' week — I believed them, and I'll print that. The money — honest." A look. "The shadow — seen. Unnamed. The paper judges. It doesn't take sides. Not yours."
> (T1 · look closer) *The proprietor looks up from the week's edition the way a judge looks up from the bench. The bluntness is the room's whole furniture. Rose takes the printing the way she takes all of Bell's verdicts: standing.* — remembered: *the printing, received.*
> (T2 · tone) *Steady: "The printed, Mrs. Bell. The true." Dry: "The judging, proprietor." Even, for the afternoon is even.* — remembered: *the steadiness, held.*
> "The treating was the week's own question. Treated — my verdict." A pause. "The shadow was the week's own question. Decided." The gravity. "The paper printed both. True."
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She hears the nodding: the true, taken. She takes the treated: the week's own, filed. She takes the decided: the shadow, priced. She holds the steadiness against the afternoon's ink-smell.* — remembered: *the true, taken.*
> (T4 · stance) *As the reader, she knows the paper's manner. As the defendant, she stands in the hearing's print. As the Hartwell, she honors the unbuyable — the paper's worth, kept.* — remembered: *the honoring, begun.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"The truth, Mrs. Bell — the whole of it?" "The judging, proprietor — and the heard?" "The sides — untaken, even mine?"* — remembered: *the honoring, done.*
> "Untaken, Miss Hartwell. Even yours. Especially yours — the town watches the favorite hardest." A pause. "The hearing is called. The paper will be there. Judging."
> (T6 · look closer) *The bluntness holds like a line held. The hearing does the calling; the paper does the judging. Rose takes the promise the way the town takes all of Bell's promises: as weather.* — remembered: *the calling, witnessed.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *With the proprietor, she takes the promise seriously, which is the only way to take it. With the paper, she honors the judging. With the afternoon, she leaves the office to its ink.* — remembered: *the honoring, done.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the judges: never-siding, filed. She keeps the unbuyable: even hers, priced. She keeps the called: the hearing, turned-toward. She keeps the office: inked, the evening's.* — remembered: *the paper, kept.*
> *(She leaves the proprietor to the desk. The presses are running below — the Gazette's heartbeat, the afternoon's. The sponsors' week printed — the believed believed, the moneyed honest, the shadow seen and unnamed — and the promise kept: the paper judges, takes no sides, prints true.)*
> *The desk keeps. The bluntness holds. And the presses run.*

scenes.synopsis: the hawk's last word — Brighton filed; the aunt's sentence, the return's. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room in the afternoon: the hawk's last word. Letitia with the sponsors' week behind her — the offers treated, the shadow decided, the return chosen. The bonnet shed, the gloves coming off, the hawk's eyes bright.)*
> "Brighton, darling." The gloves come off. "Filed. The sponsors — honest hounds, every one. The believed — the most human thing afloat. The shadow — decided." She counts on the fingers. "The week's own question — answered."
> (T1 · look closer) *The gloves come off the way last words begin. The counting is on the fingers; the brightness is the hawk's. Rose takes the last the way she takes all of Letitia's sentences: at face value, then again underneath.* — remembered: *The last, received.*
> (T2 · tone) *Dry: "Answered, Aunt." Fond, because it is Letitia. Steady, because the last wants steadiness.* — remembered: *The steadiness, held.*
> "The hearing approaches, darling." The voice lowers. "The pearls — promised. Not worn." A look. "The return's dress — the hearing's approach. Dressed, not arrived at."
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She hears the lowering: the voice, the approach. She takes the promised: the pearls, not-worn. She takes the dressed: the approach, filed. She holds the fondness for the harvester who dared.* — remembered: *The dressing, taken.*
> (T4 · stance) *As the niece, she is last-worded and dared. As the returner, she takes the approach. As the Hartwell, she files the week's sentence.* — remembered: *the wording, begun.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"The last, Aunt — filed, and the return?" "The approach, Aunt — dressed, not arrived at?" "The mercy, Aunt — the never-knowing?"* — remembered: *The asking, done.*
> "The never-knowing is kept, darling. The week's mercy." The brightness. "The town will want the romance or the ruin." The beam, wry. "The hawk keeps the filed. The filed is the last word — and the last word is Brighton's own."
> (T6 · look closer) *The beaming, then the gravity — the hawk's two weathers. Mercy does the keeping; Brighton owns the last word.* — remembered: *The keeping, witnessed.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She gives the harvester the last word's full honors, briefs her on the hearing's approach, and pours her tea — the afternoon's, sweetened, the way Letitia likes it.* — remembered: *The crowning, done.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the last: the word, filed. She keeps the filed: Brighton's, priced. She keeps the mercy: the never-knowing, kept. She keeps the aunt — the hawk of the lane.* — remembered: *The hawk, kept.*
> *(She keeps the hawk. The morning room releases her — Brighton filed, the sponsors honest hounds, the believed most human afloat, the shadow decided, the mercy kept. The town will want the romance or the ruin; the hawk keeps the filed.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — HOW TO WEAR THEM (openly, quietly, or as armor). The wearing, decided. (Turns: 3 — the decision)

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — ROSE'S TESTIMONY POSTURE (the defendant, the heir, or the witness). She decides how she stands when her name is called. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The chambers in the morning. The question: how does she stand when her name is called? She has turned it over since dawn, the way she turns a bolt of cloth before cutting — three ways to meet the room, and the room will read whichever one she wears. She can go as the accused: the claim's subject, answering it straight, humility worn plain as the pearls. She can go as the Hartwell: the house's voice, four generations standing up through her. Or she can go as the witness: the woman who chased the paper herself and can walk the room through it, page by page. All three are true. Each costs something, and she has priced all three.)*
- **The defendant** — *Answering the claim directly, in plain humility.* She stands as the accused — the law's subject, the claim met head-on and answered. (Consequence: She answers in humility; the law reads the deference, and so does the room. But the lowered head can be read as a conceding one.)
- **The heir** — *Speaking for the house, four generations behind her.* She stands as the Hartwell — the house's voice, its continuity speaking through her. (Consequence: She speaks as the Hartwell; the law reads the standing, and so does the room. But entitlement can read as unrepentance.)
- **The witness** — *Walking the room through the paper trail, page by page.* She stands as the witness — the woman who followed the trail herself, giving it straight. (Consequence: She gives it plain; the law reads the plainness, and so does the room. But plainness can read as coldness.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: whether she went as the accused, the heir, or the witness. The testimony was always going to be given. The signature is hers.)*
> *(The game remembers how she made it: the posture she took at the stand. The testimony was always going to be given; the manner of the giving is hers, and the room will know it.)*

> *(The chambers in the morning, filling. Rose watches the court assemble the way she has learned to watch rooms — once for the faces, once for the seating. The bench takes its place with the unhurried gravity of men who have done this a thousand times. The bar spreads its paper. The gallery fills with the town — and in the second row, notebook open on her knee, sits Mrs. Nance Bell: mid-forties, soft-voiced, sharp-eyed, the proprietor herself. The Gazette will cover this hearing the way it has covered the whole season: judging, never taking sides. Hugh sits with his counsel, thirty years old, courteous to the clerks, to the bench, to everyone. The sponsors hold their row behind him — moneyed men, honest in their belief, smiling. Behind the smiles stands money Rose knows about and Hugh never will. The room settles. The law has the floor.)*

> (T5 · look closer) *Bell catches her eye for exactly one second — no nod, no smile, just the sharp-eyed acknowledgment of a professional — and returns to her notebook.* — remembered: *One second of Bell's eye.*

> "Miss Hartwell. The order of it, miss. Their claim is stated first — that is their paper's privilege. Then ours: the codicils read, the ledgers entered, the testimonies taken. Both truths stated before the law. Whatever posture you chose this morning — hold it." — Quill

> (T2 · tone) *"Theirs, then ours," she says. "Posture held. Both truths." Steady, and dry enough to make him almost smile.* — remembered: *She held it steady.*
> "Exactly, miss. The ledgers entered; the testimonies taken." A pause. "Plainly, miss, and without mercy — that is my part of it. Yours is to sit still and let the paper work." — Quill
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *Theirs first, then ours — the claim, the codicils, the ledgers, the testimony. She files the order and holds the steadiness.* — remembered: *She filed the order.*
> (T4 · stance) *She sits as his client: instructed, briefed, ready. The solicitor's gravity is a garment she can wear.* — remembered: *She wore his gravity.*
> "The sequence is kept, Mr. Quill. And the posture." — Rose
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Their paper first — then the codicils, the ledgers, the truths?" "The testimonies taken in that order?" "And I sit still?"* — remembered: *She confirmed it.*
> "Just so, miss." His finger travels down the notes. "Everything entered, taken, and stated before the law — the only order the bench respects." A complete stillness. "I have never lost a case to disorder, miss. I don't intend to start today." — Quill

> (T7 · social maneuver) *She thanks him the way clients thank solicitors — briefly, and as if it were nothing, which makes it everything.* — remembered: *A brief, sufficient thanks.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *Keep the last word. Keep the order. Keep the solicitor — his gravity, his sequence, his fifty-eight years of never losing to disorder.* — remembered: *She kept the solicitor.*

> *(The chambers in the morning: the claim, stated. Hugh's counsel rises and reads — their paper, first. The entail broken a generation ago. The mortgages raised on the breaking. The late father's money poured into them year after year, in the belief the Park would one day be his. The claimant's standing, established document by document. The clerk's cadence carries it: plain, unhurried, and without the man. Hugh sits with his hands still on the table. He does not look at the paper. He looks at the room — at the bench, at the gallery, at Rose — with a pity so complete it sits in her stomach like something she ate too fast. Pity, she thinks, is worse than hatred. Hatred you can answer.)*

> (T5 · look closer) *He looks at the room, not the paper — as if the claim were a relative of his, briefly embarrassing, to be introduced and then ignored.* — remembered: *She noted the looking.*

> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *Keep the claim stated. Keep the shape: the broken entail, the raised mortgages, the poured money, the claimed standing. Keep the morning turned toward the reading.* — remembered: *She kept the claim's shape.*
> (T8 · choice) *The enduring, then — the claim stated, the paper read, the shape plain. She endures it the way she has endured all season: by listening.* — remembered: *She endured by listening.*
> *(The claim is stated, the paper read, the shape plain: the entail broken, the mortgages raised, the money poured, the standing claimed. Hugh looks at the room, not the paper, and the pity sits heavy in the air between them. The codicils come next — ours, after theirs.)*
> *(The cadence stops. The counsel sits. Quill gathers the codicils.)*

scenes.synopsis: the codicils, read — Quill's "other codicils"; the entail's true history in the paper's own voice. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The chambers in the morning: the codicils, read. Quill rises with the "other codicils" — the papers promised since the first season, the entail's true history, the last paper trail run down at last. His voice carries them the way it carries everything: plainly, and without mercy. The entail was broken a generation ago — exactly as the claimant says, exactly as the paper proves. The breaking was irregular. And the breaking was to save the estate, not to steal it. Her grandfather broke the law's paper to keep the house's stone. Both things are true at once, and the law is going to hear them both. In the gallery, Bell's pencil moves: soft-voiced, sharp-eyed, judging, never taking sides.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *Quill's voice never hurries; the clerk's pen keeps pace; Bell's pencil moves in the second row, quick and exact.* — remembered: *She heard the reading.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *The promised papers, produced. The last trail, run down. The proving exact, the mercy absent. She takes the proof and files it.* — remembered: *She filed the proof.*
> (T3 · stance) *She sits as the heir: this is her grandfather's history being read, and she owns every irregular line of it.* — remembered: *She owned the reading.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet. The gallery is writing now — every head bent, every pencil moving, the town taking notes on her grandfather's sins.* — remembered: *She let the gallery write.*
> (T5 · look closer) *Broken, irregular, saving — three facts that refuse to sit in one sentence, and the law will have to hold all three.* — remembered: *She held all three.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She keeps her eyes on Quill. The paper is hers here; she need not look away from it.* — remembered: *She kept her eyes on Quill.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *Keep the read codicils. Keep the true history: broken, irregular, to save the estate. Keep the morning turned toward the entering of the ledgers.* — remembered: *She kept the true history.*
> (T8 · choice) *The enduring, then — the codicils read, the history stated, the proving exact. She endures her grandfather's irregularity the way she has endured everything this season: in public, sitting still.* — remembered: *She endured it sitting still.*
> *(The codicils are read, the history stated, the proving exact — the entail broken, irregularly, to save the estate. The gallery writes. Bell's pencil moves, judging. The ledgers come next: Harrow's archive, in boxes, the money's road in columns.)*
> *(The cadence stops. Quill sits. Harrow's boxes come in.)*

scenes.synopsis: the paper's weight — Rackham's scattered notes entered; the obligations, the exhibits. (Turns: 8)

> *(The chambers in the morning: the paper, entered. The late Mr. Rackham's scattered notes go in as exhibits — the obligations the sixth season traced, the eighth left unguarded, the ninth season's paper — and Rose watches them go the way she has watched paper go in all season: the clerk's hands, the entered stamp, the exhibit numbers written in the margin. Each note is numbered. Each number is entered. They back the claim — and they are also the record of the money's true road, the one the cadet branch walked without knowing where it led. The paper's weight settles over the room like dust in a sunbeam: entered, numbered, weighed.)*

> (T3 · stance) *She sits as the scholar of this particular paper: nobody in the room has read Rackham longer than she has.* — remembered: *She sat as Rackham's scholar.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet. The stamp has a rhythm to it, and the rhythm is almost soothing — paper going where paper goes.* — remembered: *She found the rhythm soothing.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The notes walk toward this claim, but they walk past it too — toward the road the money actually traveled, which is not the road the claim says it traveled.* — remembered: *She noted the true road.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She watches the clerk's hands. Hands don't lie; paper only sometimes does.* — remembered: *She watched the hands.*

scenes.synopsis: the ledgers, entered — the mortgages' history; the money poured, the Park kept standing. (Turns: 8)

> *(The chambers in the morning: the ledgers, entered. Harrow's archive walks in in boxes — sixty-one years of exactness carried by two clerks — and the ledgers go in the way ledgers go in: opened, entered, numbered. The late father's money poured into the mortgages, year after year. The mortgages kept the Park standing. The entries prove it the way entries prove things: in columns, without mercy. The debt is owed to the cadets, plainly and in the record. The house belongs to the living Hartwells. The ledgers say it in the only language the law trusts, and the law is listening.)*

> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *The poured money. The standing Park. The law's only language. The distinction — the debt owed, the house kept. She takes the distinction and files it.* — remembered: *She filed the distinction.*
> (T3 · stance) *She sits as the heir: this is her money's history too, the columns her inheritance in ink.* — remembered: *She sat as the heir.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet. Harrow's sixty-one years of exactness are having their day in court, and the old historian would hate every minute of the attention.* — remembered: *She spared him a wry thought.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The entries don't argue. They don't pity. They state: so much paid, in such years, to keep the roof on. Columns are merciless, and that is their virtue.* — remembered: *She noted the columns' virtue.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She nods once toward Harrow's boxes — the archive honored, the keeping acknowledged.* — remembered: *She honored the archive.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *Keep the entered ledgers. Keep the proved columns. Keep the morning turned toward the stand — Hugh to testify, and the treatment to be chosen.* — remembered: *She kept the ledgers.*
> (T8 · choice) *The proving, then — the ledgers entered, the history proved in columns, the distinction drawn: the money kept the Park standing, and the keeping is owed. She proves it the way the ledgers prove it: without raising her voice.* — remembered: *She proved it quietly.*
> *(The ledgers are entered, the history proved, the distinction drawn — the money poured, the Park kept standing, the debt owed to the cadets, the house the Hartwells'. Hugh is to take the stand, and how she meets him there is the next choice.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — HOW TO TREAT HUGH ON THE STAND (with severity, with courtesy, or with candor). She decides the manner. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The chambers at midday: the question of how she meets Hugh on the stand. He is about to testify — thirty years old, courteous, pitying her — and she has to decide the manner of it before he sits down. She can meet him with severity: his testimony answered as the claim's opponent, paper against paper, the stand treated as a field. She can meet him with courtesy: as the cousin, grace extended under the law's eyes. Or she can meet him with candor: plainly, the pity answered with plainness, the truth spoken eye to eye. Each is honest. Each changes the hearing — and the man, who is not a villain, will feel whichever she chooses.)*
- **With severity** — *Paper against paper; the stand treated as a field.* She meets his testimony as the opponent — paper answered with paper, the stand a field. (Consequence: The law reads her rigor, and the room reads it. But the stand-as-field is war's grammar, and war's grammar can wound the human.)
- **With courtesy** — *Grace extended, cousin to cousin, under the law's eyes.* She meets him as the cousin — grace extended whole, the courtesy complete. (Consequence: The law reads her grace, and the room reads it. But softness can read as concession.)
- **With candor** — *Plainly: his pity answered with plainness, eye to eye.* She meets him plainly — the pity answered with plainness, nothing dressed up. (Consequence: The law reads her plainness, and the room reads it. But plainness is unguarded, and every eye will price it.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and how she met him: with severity, with courtesy, or with candor. Hugh was always going to take the stand. The manner of the meeting is hers, and he will carry it out of the courtroom with him.)*

It is duty, and love of the house. He does not hate Rose. He pities her — and that is worse, because pity has no handle to grip. He never knows whose money stands behind his sponsors' smiles. > *(The chambers at midday: the cross, handled. Hugh's answers are the man's: duty, love of the house, the father's story. > (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *Exactly, without mercy — and without touching the humanity. The treatment chosen rides behind every question. She holds it there.* — remembered: *She held the treatment.*
> (T3 · stance) *She sits as the client: the cross is Quill's instrument, and she lets him play it.* — remembered: *She let him play.*

scenes.synopsis: the hearing's ritual — dress the defendant for the law's day; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda; the pearls worn, the ritual dresses around them. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "The hearing. Both truths will be stated in open court, and the bench will watch the defendant as closely as the evidence. Dress severe: charcoal, iron-grey, or black. The gown argues exactly one thing — that the woman inside it honors the law. The pearls are worn; the whole ritual dresses around the grandmother's rope. No ornament a judge could mistake for an appeal. Serious colors only. **Editorial criterion: law-dressing.**"
>
> **A. The Severe** — charcoal silk, severe; the law dressed plain. Motif: a restrained line at the waist — severity embroidered, nothing past it. Thread: **silver** (the edge) / **charcoal silk** (the match) / **none** (plain). Colorway: charcoal + silver. Accessories: the grandmother's pearl rope, worn; the pearl drops, worn; charcoal kid gloves, plain; one white lily at the wrist.
> **B. The Defendant** — iron-grey wool silk, worked; the woman on trial dressed as herself. Motif: patience, restrained — the papers' own patience, stitched in. Thread: **steel** (the edge) / **iron-grey silk** (the match) / **matching silk** (plain). Colorway: iron-grey + steel. Accessories: the grandmother's pearl rope, worn; the pearl drops, worn; grey kid gloves, plain; one white lily at the wrist.
> **C. The Unassailable** — black silk, plain; a defense that needs no decoration. Motif: plainness — virtue unembroidered. Thread: **silver** (the edge) / **jet** (the lining) / **matching silk** (exact). Colorway: black + silver. Accessories: the grandmother's pearl rope, worn; the pearl drops, worn; black kid gloves, plain; one white lily at the wrist.
>
> *(The dressing room on the hearing's morning, before six. The lily waits in a glass of water, one stem, already cut. The rope is already at her throat — she put it on first, before the shift, the way other women put on their luck. On the tray, the pins Élise laid out in a soldier's row. The mirror stands covered with a cloth; it will be consulted once, and briefly.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *Three gowns hang where Élise left them: charcoal, iron-grey, black. The pearls are already worn, and every choice now is a frame built around the rope. She chooses the way she chooses counsel — for the room it must convince. The severe, the defendant, or the unassailable. **Direction.** The case is heard today, both truths stated. Dress to honor the bench, not to move the gallery. **Editorial criterion.** Law-dressing — every pin must answer the law's eyes, not the town's.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the hearing. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never as a step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** *The chosen gown comes off its hanger and over her head in one practiced movement. The silk falls to the floor in a single unbroken line. Severe means exactly this: nothing for the eye to catch on except the pearls.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Neckline, the rope's:** *The neckline is cut to frame the rope and do nothing else. The pearls sit where they have sat all morning, cool at first, then warm against her skin. The gown keeps quiet around them.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — The rope, checked:** *The clasp at the nape, checked with a fingertip, then checked again. The grandmother's rope lies exactly where it lay at the ball, the christening, the solicitor's office — worn to every battle of this season, and the law's day is no exception.* *5 coins.*
> *(The pins accumulate on the tray in Élise's soldier row, each one set and spent. The dressing room holds its early light the way the courtroom will hold its hush: without comment.)*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — The drops, checked:** *The pearl drops, the pair, each in its ear. She gives her head one sharp shake, the way she used to test a girth. Nothing moves. They will not fly off in the witness box.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Fit, severe:** *No rustle, no train, no swishing past the counsel's table. Élise took the skirt in until it walks like a clerk's. The law's walk is unheard; she intends to be heard some other way.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** *Long to the wrist — the season's habit and the courtroom's both. Her wrists will be bare of everything but the lily's stem.* *5 coins.*
> *(The drops sit steady, the sleeves lie flat, and the day leans closer. Somewhere below, the carriage is being brought round; she hears the harness before she hears the wheels.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Hair, coiled severe:** *The braid coiled tight and pinned to the skull. "Severe suits you," Letitia said once, meaning it suited nobody else. No strand will escape to soften her in the gallery's eyes.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Gloves, plain:** *Plain kid, no buttons, no embroidery. Her hands will be seen handling papers, not fluttering. Gloves are the courtroom's punctuation: full stops, not flourishes.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Lily, one stem:** *The white lily, one stem, bound at the wrist with a thread of the gown's own silk. Purity of intent, the flower books say. She doubts the bench reads flower books, but Augusta would notice its absence, and that is audience enough.* *5 coins.*
> *(Severe hair, plain gloves, the lily's stem — the dressing room is starting to look like a courtroom already, all of it unadorned and all of it deliberate.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** *No scent. The chambers will smell of dust, old wood, and counsel's papers; she will add nothing to it. A perfume in a courtroom is an argument, and she has arguments enough.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Posture, straight:** *Shoulders back, chin level — the spine the dancing master billed for, finally earning its fee. The gown hangs straighter when the woman inside it stands like a witness.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Gaze, level:** *Level, for the bench. Not down — down is the gallery's pity, and she will not buy it. Not up — up is defiance, and defiance loses cases. Level: the eyes of a woman answering questions she has already answered in writing.* *5 coins.*
> *(The spine straightens, the gaze settles, and she allows herself one glance at the covered mirror. Not yet. The cloth stays on until the ritual is done — superstition, and she is not above it.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Voice, even:** *She tries a sentence aloud — "Good morning" — and hears it come out even, lower than her ballroom voice. The severe voice. It will carry across a courtroom without rising, which is the whole point of it.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Hands, still:** *Still. The pearl at her throat is the one thing she may touch, and only when the testimony runs long. Her hands fold, unfold, and settle. Stillness is the last ornament.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Step, measured:** *She crosses the dressing room once, heel to toe, counting nothing. Measured: the walk of a woman who has somewhere to be and no need to hurry toward it.* *5 coins.*
> *(Level gaze, even voice, still hands — the hearing's instruments, tuned. Below, the carriage wheels stop being heard and start being waited for.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Nod, once:** *For the bench, when the time comes: one nod, and no more. A nod given twice is a curtsy, and she is curtsying to no one today.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, none:** *No smile. A smile in the dock is read three ways by three papers, and all of them wrong. Her mouth rests in its natural line — what Letitia calls her courtroom face, which is really just her face.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Turn, away:** *She turns from the covered mirror without uncovering it — the ritual's own discipline. She will see herself in the courtroom's eyes soon enough, and they will be less kind.* *5 coins.*
> *(One nod, no smile, the turn away — the dressing room's grammar is fluent now. The pins on the tray are gone; the soldier's row has marched.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Door, held:** *Her hand on the door handle, held a breath. The dressing room behind her is tidy as a ledger: every pin spent, every choice entered. Whatever waits past this door, the morning's arithmetic is done.* *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — Threshold, crossed:** *She crosses it with the pearls at her throat and the lily at her wrist. The stairs, the hall, the carriage door, the courtroom doors after that — each threshold the same size, each one crossed the same way. The day has its armor.* *5 coins.*
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. The completed direction is remembered. Owned jewels may be added freely from the open shelf, never as a step. No Crown SKU touches the ritual.)*
> *(Story morsel: the housemaid, laying out the lily the night before: "The law's day, ma'am." A pause, the stem set in water. "You'll want the flower, ma'am." She had not asked for it. The girl had read the room the way good servants read weather.)*
> *(Story morsel: a card slipped under the door before dawn, Augusta's hand — "Severe, child. The law respects the severe, and the town respects the law." She pins it inside the wardrobe door, where it will be the last thing she sees.)*
> *(Story morsel: the morning Gazette, read aloud over the pinning of the hair — Bell on the hearing's day, even and unsparing. "The court sits at ten. The paper will be there." A beat. "The paper is always there.")*
> *(The coda — the mirror)* *The cloth comes off the mirror, and it is consulted once, briefly. The woman in it is severe from the braid to the hem, and at her throat the grandmother's pearls — the one warm thing in the whole composition, and the truest. She touches the rope once, the way she touched the ledger's ink: to be sure it is real. Then the dressing room releases her, and the bench waits.*
