scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — HOW TO FACE THE TON (attend everything, attend nothing, or attend once). The facing, decided. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library in the morning: the week's first question, and it won't wait for the second cup of tea. She lays the invitations in three rows on the desk and prices the roads the way she prices everything now — by cost and by what they buy. Attend everything: be seen in every room, every tea, every evening, the defendant's face worn openly — nerve as the argument, the town reading the nerve all week. Attend nothing: the house her fortress, the shutters of her own making; the town tries the case without the defendant and writes its own account of her absence. Attend once: one evening, the one that matters — stake the whole week on a single night and let the one appearance be the whole statement. Each road meets the ton. Each meets it differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — How to Face the Ton:*
- **Attend everything** — *show up everywhere, all week, and let nerve be the argument.* She goes everywhere — every room, every tea, every evening, the face worn openly. (Consequence: the town reads the nerve all week — but going everywhere is going exposed, and any room can price an exposed woman.)
- **Attend nothing** — *stay home behind her own shutters; let dignity be the argument.* She goes nowhere — the house her fortress, the trial tried in her absence. (Consequence: total dignity, total absence — but silence lets the town answer for her.)
- **Attend once** — *one evening, the one that matters; stake the whole week on it.* She goes once — the one evening that matters, the week's whole argument. (Consequence: the appearance is the statement — but one night is a gamble, and it stakes the week.)
> *(She makes the choice, and the game keeps the manner of it — everywhere, nowhere, or once. The ton was always going to try the week; the part that is hers is how she walks through it.)*

Abandon him: leave him to the town's weighing unchampioned, the courtesy she was shown returned with silence, and let the town answer for her. Stand apart: his standing the town's business, hers the hearing's — step outside the question and let both verdicts fall where they fall. His father's money kept the Park standing; the money is owed as a debt, not the house. That is the law's column. The town's column is still being written. Each road places her. > *(She makes the choice, and the game keeps the manner of it — the defense, the silence, or the standing apart. Hugh was always going to be weighed; the part that is hers is where she stands while it happens.)*

> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes the kept — the laughing, the portrait, the true exhibit — and the refused offering, and holds them together. Some things the town cannot weigh because they are not for sale.* — remembered: *Kept taken; not for sale.*

> *(The library, night: the week's last question. The ball is danced, the drawing rooms have spoken, and the week is ending the way weeks end — all at once, and then slowly. She prices the roads. The verdict sought: go after the drawing rooms' verdict, hear it named to her face, face it whole — nerve as the answer, whatever the naming costs. The verdict shunned: let the town's verdict pass unnamed, unheard, the week's trial closed without its reading — pride as the answer, and the town left to talk to itself. The verdict outlasted: outlast them both, the week's and the season's — the pearls rested all week and polished for the morrow, the outlasting made visible. Each road ends the week. Each ends it differently.)*

> *(She makes the choice, and the game keeps the manner of it — the seeking, the shunning, or the outlasting. The week was always going to end; the part that is hers is how she closes it.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — HOW TO CARRY THE FLOWER (wear them, send them, or let them stand). The carrying is chosen; the week takes its flower. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The drawing room, night. The lilies stand in the tall glasses, the buds beginning to think about opening. The question the night demands: how does she carry the season's flower through the verdict's week? She prices the roads the way she prices everything — once for the gesture, once for the consequence. To wear them: a sprig at the bosom, the flower on her person, the unassailable worn where the town looks first. To send them: bouquets out into the town, the flower carried by other hands, the purity delivered. To let them stand: the tall glasses in the drawing room, the flower kept at home, the week's campaign conducted from the house. Each road carries the lily. Each seasons the week differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — How to Carry the Flower:*
- **Wear them** — *worn at the bosom, where the town looks first.* She wears the lilies — a sprig at the bosom, the flower on her person, where the town looks first. (Consequence: the town sees the flower on her — the unassailable worn openly; but worn flowers wilt, and the town notices wilting.)
- **Send them** — *bouquets out into the town, carried by other hands.* She sends the lilies — bouquets out into the town, the purity carried by other hands. (Consequence: the flower travels — the week's campaign conducted abroad; but sent flowers are read as messages, and messages are answered.)
- **Let them stand** — *kept at home, in the drawing room's tall glasses.* She lets them stand — the tall glasses in the drawing room, the campaign conducted from home. (Consequence: the house holds the flower — the unassailable at its most unmoved; but standing flowers are seen only by callers, and callers are fewer in a waiting week.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the wearer, the sender, or the keeper. The week was always going to be flowered. The carrying is hers, and the night keeps her counsel while she chooses.)*

scenes.synopsis: the lilies' ritual — dress the flower's week; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "The verdict's week — the waiting days, the callers' afternoons, the flower carried. The dress code of the flowered: white, severe, and honest. Lilies may be worn, sent, or left standing in the drawing room — always meant. Nothing wilting, nothing loud. Dark colors permitted; the flower does the arguing. **Editorial criterion: purity.**"
>
> **A. The Worn** — white muslin, flowered and sprigged. Motif: the lily, embroidered in whitework, small at the hem. Thread: **whitework** (purity, stated plainly) / **silver** (edged, unassailable) / **matching silk** (exact, invisible). Colorway: white + silver + pearl grey. Accessories: the pearl lily-drop; a fresh sprig at the bosom; white kid gloves.
> **B. The Sent** — pearl grey, severe and unadorned. Motif: plainness, worn without apology. Thread: **matching silk** (exact) / **jet** (edged) / **none** (plain, and proud of it). Colorway: pearl grey + ash + jet. Accessories: the bouquet's ribbon, kept in the reticule; the card case; plain grey kid gloves.
> **C. The Standing** — dove silk, quiet, for at home. Motif: the Hartwell oak, restrained and small. Thread: **dove silk** (matched) / **silver** (edged) / **whitework** (quiet, lit from within). Colorway: dove + silver + white. Accessories: the conservatory key on its ribbon, kept; pearl drops; the wool shawl for the evening chill.
>
> *(The dressing room, first light: the lilies' week begins on a hanger. Three rows on the rail — the white, the grey, the dove — and she thinks, briefly and practically, of laundry.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits before the mirror is consulted — the worn, the sent, or the standing. The hair, severe. Everything else restrained. **Direction.** The verdict's week: the waiting days, the callers' afternoons. Dress to be unassailable. **Editorial criterion.** Purity — every choice answers the flower, not the ballroom.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the flower's week. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** the week chooses the gown — white flowered muslin, or pearl grey severe, or dove silk quiet. She lifts it off the rail and the hanger swings empty; the choice is made. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, exact:** fitted exact, not tight. No rustle for the callers' ears, no train for the stairs. She moves in it once across the boards, and it makes no argument. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** long sleeves, the writing habit — the afternoons will be spent at the callers' table with a pen, and cuffs take ink better than wrists. *5 coins.*
> *(The gown's line is set, the sleeves long for the letter-writing afternoons — and the dressing room holds its morning light the way the drawing room downstairs holds the lilies: patiently.)*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, high:** high, for the unassailable. The week's fashion is seriousness, worn at the throat. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, coiled:** coiled and pinned, every strand accounted for. Her grandmother's severity, borrowed for the week and returned on Sunday. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Reticule, packed:** the notebook, the pencil, and the spare tucked behind her ear the way she has carried one since she was sixteen. A handkerchief. Nothing in it rattles. *5 coins.*
> *(The hair severe, the reticule packed without a rattle — and the week leans in, the callers already at their tea.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, plain:** plain kid, white or grey to the gown. Flowers are handled, not displayed; the gloves come off for the lilies. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Boots, quiet:** quiet boots for the stairs and the callers' floors. She tests them — two steps on the boards, no sound. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Shawl, wool:** the wool shawl for the evening chill. Wool, not cashmere. The week is not for softness. *5 coins.*
> *(Quiet boots, plain gloves — the week's houses ask for the unheard, and she is happy to oblige.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, small:** the small silver lily brooch, pinned where the fresh sprig will sit. Unshowy. It catches the light once, and then behaves. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** no perfume. The lilies downstairs are doing all the smelling for the house. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, straight:** straight. She has carried trays, ledgers, and one memorable spring; she can carry a spine. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine straightens, the brooch behaves — and the mirror gets its brief consultation from the corner of her eye.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, level:** level. Met eye to eye across the callers' table — neither dropped, nor challenging. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, even:** even, for the waiting. The flower answers questions; the lady answers them once. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, still:** still. The lilies are carried, not fidgeted with. She folds her hands once, and they stay folded. *5 coins.*
> *(Level gaze, even voice, still hands — the week's instruments, tuned for the waiting.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, measured:** measured, for the stairs and the long afternoons. No hurry. Hurry is a confession. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, rare:** rare, and therefore spent like coin. She prices it accordingly. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Nod, once:** once, for the caller's answer. The nod is taken, the matter closed, the tea refilled. *5 coins.*
> *(The step measured, the smile rare, the nod once — the grammar of waiting, spoken fluently.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Turn, away:** away, when the call is done. She turns at the door, not before; the week is not dismissed mid-sentence. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — Door, held:** held, for the next caller. The week is dressed, the flower carried, the room ready. *5 coins.*
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. The completed direction is remembered. Owned jewels may be added freely from the open shelf, never as a step. No Crown SKU touches the ritual.)*
> *(Story morsel: the brass-polisher's boy on the stairs, cloth never pausing — "The deciding's elsewhere, ma'am," he says, and polishes on. She takes the stairs a half-step lighter.)*
> *(Story morsel: a card slipped under the door in Letitia's hand — "Unassailable, darling. By bloom." She pins it inside the wardrobe door, where it will be the last thing she sees.)*
> *(Story morsel: the morning Gazette, read aloud over the pinning — Bell on the waiting, dry and not unkind. "The town waits, miss. The law thinks. The lilies stand. I am watching." The maid pins faster.)*
> *(The coda — the mirror)* *She consults it briefly, and it answers: white, severe, meant. The dressing room lets her go. The callers are waiting.*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — WHAT THEY DECLARE (purity, defiance, or peace). The declaration is chosen; the lilies speak. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The drawing room, night. The lilies fully open, the scent whole and unhurried, the verdict's eve arrived. The question the night demands — the week's last: what do the lilies declare? She prices the roads the way she has priced everything this week — once for the gesture, once for the consequence. Purity: the flower's own meaning, the unassailable stated plain, the defendant's innocence of strategy declared. Defiance: the town's reading made hers, the flower as armor acknowledged, the waiting's steel shown. Peace: the week's quietest road, the flower as olive-branch, the verdict awaited without a weapon in hand. Each road declares. Each seasons the morrow differently. The evening waits on her choosing, the way evenings have waited all week.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — What They Declare:*
- **Purity** — *the flower's own meaning, stated plainly.* She declares purity — the flower's own meaning, the unassailable stated plain. (Consequence: the town hears innocence — the defendant's strategy declared as none; but purity claimed is purity tested, and the morrow will test everything.)
- **Defiance** — *the town's reading, made hers.* She declares defiance — the town's reading made hers, the flower as armor acknowledged. (Consequence: the town hears steel — the waiting's nerve shown openly; but defiance declared is defiance answered, and the law answers in its own language.)
- **Peace** — *the olive branch, offered unarmed.* She declares peace — the week's quietest road, the flower as olive-branch, the verdict awaited without a weapon in hand. (Consequence: the town hears quiet — the unarmed awaited; but peace declared before a verdict is read as confidence, and confidence is read as provocation by those who want it so.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the pure, the defiant, or the peaceful. The lilies were always going to speak. The declaration is hers, and the night keeps her counsel while she makes it. The lilies wait in their glasses, patient as declarations.)*

scenes.synopsis: Bell on the lilies — the sting, read once over chocolate; the paper's verdict on the flowered week. (Turns: 1 — the reading)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning Gazette, read over chocolate. Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, in her own dry voice — soft, sharp, and blunt as a paperknife:)*
> *"The town waited, and the defendant flowered. White lilies — worn, sent, standing — the week's whole argument made of petals. Half the town read purity in them, half read defiance; both halves were reading themselves, as is the town's habit. Nothing hides in a lily — that is the flower's whole trick, and the lady's, if she means it. But a flower is a promise, not a proof. The law names the morrow, and the morrow will do the proving. The Gazette will read the naming. We judge here. We do not carry."*
> (T1 · stance) *Rose reads it twice — the satisfaction first (the flowered week, judged in print as well as in company), then the second reading, which is Bell's real gift: the paper has not declared her pure. It has declared the question open, and set the terms. Formidable terms. Permanent ones.* — remembered: *the lesson: the judging paper carries nothing, and judges everything.*

scenes.prose:
> *(The appointed hour arrives in a room that smells of sealing-wax and damp wool. The clerk reads the judgment in the flat voice of a man paid to be forgotten. First the entail's breaking, acknowledged: the grandfather's doing, and the necessity's. Then the mortgages, entry by entry, year by year: the cadet branch's money, Hugh's father's money, poured in to keep the roof on Hartwell Park. And last, the naming. Hugh Hartwell is owed a debt, handsomely measured. He is not owed the house. The house is hers. Beyond challenge. Forever.)*

scenes.synopsis: Bell on the debt — the sting, read; the paper's verdict on the naming's week. (Turns: 1 — the reading)

> *(The morning Gazette, read over chocolate. Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, in her own dry voice:)*
> *"The law named a debt, and the lady named it handsomely. The cadet branch's money — poured year by year into the mortgages, keeping the roof on — is owed, and will be paid, and the paying will be handsome in words the law did not require. The father's name stands cleared in the record, and will stand cut in the Park's stone. The house is not owed. The house is entire — named so, in the lady's own words, and the naming is the week's whole argument. The Gazette judges the naming well done, and does not applaud it. The paper judges. It does not carry."*

She files the sting under its lesson: in London, the paper that judges the handsome without applauding it is the only paper worth being judged by.* — remembered: *the lesson: the judging paper applauds nothing, and judges everything.*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE SHAPE OF MERCY (for Hugh, for the fathers, or for herself). The mercy is shaped; the terms will follow. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The drawing room, night. The lilies stand in the tall glasses, white and unhurried. The blank pages wait on the table, patient as Quill promised. Somewhere below, the house settles for the night: a door latched, a footman's step on the stair, the embers dropping in the grate. The question the night asks is the week's first: what shape does the mercy take? She runs the three roads in her mind. For Hugh: grace given where it can be received, by the living cousin at the table. For the fathers: grace given where it can only be remembered, the breaking understood, the money honored. For herself: grace given where it has been longest withheld, the defendant's posture set down at last. Each road shapes the mercy. Each seasons the terms differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The Shape of Mercy:*
- **For Hugh** — *grace for the living, received where it can be received.* She shapes the mercy for Hugh — toward the living cousin, the terms generous to the man at the table. (Consequence: the cousin receives — grace given where it can be received, the living honored; but mercy to the living is read as concession, and the town reads everything.)
- **For the fathers** — *grace for the dead, remembered where it cannot answer.* She shapes the mercy for the fathers — the breaking understood, the money honored, grace where it can only be remembered. (Consequence: the dead are honored — the fathers weighed entire, the past settled; but the dead cannot answer, and the living watch the settling.)
- **For herself** — *grace for herself, the posture set down at last.* She shapes the mercy for herself — the posture set down, the armor laid aside, grace where longest withheld. (Consequence: the woman is freed — the defendant's weight lifted, the season's armor laid down; but mercy to oneself is the hardest to name, and the town names it selfishness.)
> *(The candle burns low in the tall glasses' shadow. The lilies do not hurry her. The blank pages do not hurry her. The pen lies where she left it. The house sleeps above her, and the three roads keep until morning.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE DEBT'S PUBLIC NAMING (how publicly: the Gazette, the ton, or the assembly). The debt is named; decide how widely the naming carries. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library, night, the lamp turned low. The first head stands acknowledged, and the naming has come due — the paying was never in question; the naming of the paying is the whole of the art. The question is how widely the paying is named, and in whose mouth. She prices the roads the way Augusta taught her, one by one. The Gazette: name it in the paper, Bell's own verdict on the paying, the ton reading it over breakfast with the toast. The ton: name it in the drawing rooms, the town's own mouths carrying it from sofa to sofa, the whispers doing the work the ink cannot. The assembly: name it at the settlement assembly itself, the paying done before witnesses, the day watching and the watching remembered. Each road names the debt. Each seasons the handsome differently, and the seasoning is the choice.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The Debt's Public Naming:*
- **Name it in the Gazette** — *Ink on paper: Bell's verdict, read over breakfast.* She names the debt in the paper — Bell's verdict on the paying, the ton reading it over breakfast, the naming's whole grammar. (Consequence: the named is printed — the paying is priced where all London reads it, and the reading is the whole art; but the paper judges, it never takes sides, and Bell's verdict is hers to write, not Rose's to buy.)
- **Name it in the ton** — *Drawing-room talk: the whispers carry it, sofa to sofa.* She names the debt in the drawing rooms — the ton's own mouths carrying it, the whispers' whole grammar. (Consequence: the named is carried — the paying is priced where the ton talks, and the talking is the whole art; but the ton's mouths change the adjectives, and the handsome may shrink in the retelling.)
- **Name it at the assembly** — *Before witnesses: the paying done in the open, the day watching.* She names the debt at the settlement assembly — the paying done before witnesses entire, the day's whole grammar. (Consequence: the named is witnessed — the paying is priced where the day watches, and the watching is the whole art; but the assembly waits, and the ton will have named it first in its own way.)
> *(The game remembers the choice, and the means: the printer, the whisperer, or the witness. The debt was always going to be paid. The naming is hers, and the seasoning with it.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE STONE'S WORDING (how Hugh's father's name is cut: plainly, nobly, or with the keeping's words). The stone waits; decide what the cutting carries. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The mason's yard, afternoon, the choosing come due at last. The second head stands cleared, the father's name, in the record, black on white. The stone waits in its row, and the question is what it carries besides the name — for stone keeps longest, and what is cut is cut. She prices the roads the way Harrow taught her, with the ledger open in her head. Plainly: the name cut plainly, the name and nothing else, the stone's own grammar, silence doing the rest. Nobly: the name cut with his Hartwell style, the station stated, the family's grammar, blood answering for keeping. The keeping's words: the name cut with the keeping's words, the poured and the stood named in the stone's own tongue, the archive's grammar, long but true. Each road cuts the name. Each seasons the clearing differently, and the seasoning is hers to choose.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The Stone's Wording:*
- **Cut it plainly** — *The name alone, cut clean, nothing beside it.* She cuts the name plainly — the name and nothing else, the stone's own grammar. (Consequence: the plain is entire — the name is priced where stone keeps longest, and the keeping is the whole art; but the plain says nothing of the poured, and the ton may read the silence however the ton pleases.)
- **Cut it nobly** — *His Hartwell style beside the name: the station stated.* She cuts the name with his Hartwell style — the station stated, the family's whole grammar. (Consequence: the noble is entire — the station is priced where the family reads it, and the reading is the whole art; but the noble claims the blood, and the blood was never the keeping's whole story.)

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE DEBT'S PAYING (how the debt is paid: how handsomely, how publicly). The paying waits; decide the manner of the payment. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The study, morning: the paying come due. The debt stands named — the books agree on the sum, the creditor's name is written fair, the draft waits in her pocket — and the settlement assembly will witness its discharge within the hour. The question is only the manner of it, and she turns the three ways of paying over the way she turns everything: slowly, and with the consequences laid out beside them like cards. Handsomely and publicly — the payment made before the whole assembly, generously, where all can see, the county carrying the story home. Handsomely and quietly — paid in full, without display, the dignity of the thing needing no witness, the books speaking for themselves. Exactly and publicly — paid to the sum before the assembly, precise to the shilling, and accounted, no man able to call it short. Each way pays the debt. Each way tells the ton a different story about the payer, and the ton will tell it for years.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The Debt's Paying:*
- **Handsomely and publicly** — *paid generously, before the whole assembly.* She pays the debt handsomely and publicly — before the whole assembly, the generosity entire. (Consequence: the paid is generous — the settlement is priced where the assembly witnesses the handsome, and the witnessing is the whole art; but the handsome is large, and the ton may read the large as the buying's.)
- **Handsomely and quietly** — *paid generously, with no display.* She pays the debt handsomely and quietly — the dignity entire, without display. (Consequence: the paid is dignified — the settlement is priced where the handsome needs no witness, and the needing-none is the whole art; but the quiet is private, and the ton may read the private as the hiding's.)
- **Exactly and publicly** — *paid to the exact sum, before the assembly.* She pays the debt exactly and publicly — to the sum, before the assembly, the precision entire. (Consequence: the paid is precise — the settlement is priced where the assembly witnesses the exact, and the witnessing is the whole art; but the exact is measured, and the ton may read the measured as the grudging's.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the manner: the handsome-public, the handsome-quiet, or the exact-public. The debt was always going to be paid. The manner is hers.)*

scenes.prose:
> *(The Park, mid-morning: the cutting come due. The stone stands worded — Hugh's father's name chalked fair, the clearing spoken before the assembly, the ring of witnesses waiting on the rise — and the mason waits with his tools laid out on the cloth, the chisel clean, the mallet ready, his cap in his hand. The question is only how the cutting is done, and she turns the three ways over slowly, with the assembly waiting. With witnesses — the cutting done before them all, the whole county watching the letters stand, none able to say it was done in a corner. With words — the cutting done with the clearing spoken aloud as the chisel strikes, the name said and cut together in a single act. In silence — the cutting done without a word, the stone and the chisel speaking for themselves, grave before the crowd. Each way cuts the stone. Each way tells a different story about the clearing, and Hugh will carry whichever story she chooses.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The Stone's Cutting:*
- **With witnesses** — *cut before the whole assembly's eyes.* She cuts the stone with witnesses — before the whole assembly, the seen entire. (Consequence: the cut is witnessed — the clearing is priced where the assembly sees the stone cut, and the seeing is the whole art; but the witnessed is public, and the ton may read the public as the performance's.)

(Consequence: the cut is worded — the clearing is priced where the speaking accompanies the stone, and the accompanying is the whole art; but the worded is declared, and the ton may read the declared as the verdict's.)
- **In silence** — *cut without a word spoken.* She cuts the stone in silence — the unspoken, the silent entire. (Consequence: the cut is silent — the clearing is priced where the stone is cut without a word, and the wordlessness is the whole art; but the silent is quiet, and the ton may read the quiet as the withholding's.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the manner: the witnessed, the worded, or the silent. The stone was always going to be cut. The manner is hers.)*

The wearing was hers. The evening is hers too.)*

scenes.synopsis: Élise's final bow — the discipline honored entire; twenty-two, entire. (Turns: 8)

> *(The atelier, evening: the modiste's final bow. The verdict gown has been worn — stated, absolute, the settlement's reading done — and Élise stands in the quiet workshop with her hands folded, twenty-two, steady, the honesty entire. The needles are at rest, the shears hung, the tall glasses in the hall holding the lilies she cut at dawn. The scarred workshop did its most disciplined work, and the work was worn at the settlement. The discipline is honored.)*
> "Miss." She looks up — the eyes warm and level, the pins long out of her mouth. "Worn." A pause. "The verdict gown." The warm certainty. "The settlement's reading — done." A look. "Stitch by stitch, it held." — Élise

> (T2 · tone) *Warm: "Worn, Élise — and it held. Every seam, every hour. The assembly read it, and the stone was cut under its eye."* — remembered: *Shown: the fondness — and the stone cut under the gown's eye.*
> "Held." She bows — the modiste's bow, deep and plain. "The season — settled." A look up. "The Park — yours." Another pause, and the honesty entire: "Beyond challenge." — Élise
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose takes the beyond-challenge from the girl's mouth — the workshop's verdict on the morning — and sets it with the Dowager's.* — remembered: *Taken: the beyond-challenge — the workshop's verdict, set with the Dowager's.*

> "Done, Élise — the honoring is done, and now the friendship. The season was the workshop's too. Sit with me a moment — the atelier is quiet, and the evening is ours." — Rose
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Ours, miss —" "Ours. The discipline, the seams, the vanity-checking — all of it." "The third checking," she says, and smiles properly for the first time all day. > "Mattered." The bow deepens into something warmer — the twenty-two entire, the girl and the modiste both. "Wear it hard, miss — you did. I watched from the doorway." — Élise
> (T6 · look closer) *The smile stays this time; the day's proof has loosened something in her.* — remembered: *Marked: the loosening — the day's proof, the smile staying.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *They sit together among the silk scraps, patron and modiste, and drink the tea the girl makes — too strong, and perfect.* — remembered: *Shared: the tea — too strong, and perfect, among the silk scraps.*

> *(The workshop settles around them — the shears hung, the needles at rest — and Élise, twenty-two, pours the tea too strong and does not apologize for it. The discipline is honored. The evening is theirs.)*

scenes.synopsis: Octavia's keeping — the settlement sketched; the sketched, the kept. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The studio, evening: Octavia with the settlement sketched. Thirty-four, precise, the devotion entire — she has spent the day the way she spends everything: quickly, and with love, her charcoal moving over the paper. The verdict gown was sketched before it was worn; the debt's paying sketched as it happened; the stone's cutting sketched from the rise. The debt was paid, the name was cut, the Park is hers — and the studio holds the day in a dozen sheets, pinned to the boards. She looks up as Rose comes in, her hand finding Rose's without looking.)*
> "Rose." The hand tightens — warm, charcoal-smudged. "The settlement — sketched." A pause. "The three — executed." A look, the painter's gravity. "The debt — paid. The stone —" her voice steadies — "cut. The name — cleared." Another pause. "The Park — yours." — Octavia

> (T2 · tone) *Warm: "Sketched, Octavia — the whole settlement? Before it was settled?"* — remembered: *Shown: the fondness — the whole settlement, sketched before it was settled.*
> "Before, during, and after." A nod — the precision entire. "The waiting — in cloth and ink. The cutting — in line and shadow." She looks at the boards. "The season's last day, Rose — drawn while it happened, that it might be kept." — Octavia
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose takes the keeping as it is offered — the studio's answer to the settlement — and honors it.* — remembered: *Taken: the keeping — the studio's answer to the settlement.*
> (T4 · stance) *As the beloved she receives the sketches; as the friend she understands what they cost.* — remembered: *Received: the sketches — and the knowing of what they cost.*
> "Kept, Octavia — the settlement is kept, and the keeping is the answer. The sketch holds what the settling could not say." — Rose

> *(The house, evening: Henry with the settlement stood. Thirty-three, the honor entire, the uniform still immaculate after the long day — he has stood it the way he stands everything: plainly, and without complaint. The three terms have executed — the debt paid, the name cut, the Park hers. The standing was his to do. The standing is done.)*
> "Rose." He bows — the soldier's bow, back straight as the morning. "The settlement — settled." A pause. "The three — executed." A look. "The debt — paid." The steadiness holds. "The name — cut." The honor's full weight. "The Park — yours." Another pause. "The standing was mine to do, Rose." — Henry

> "Stood." The honor holds — the thirty-three entire. "In uniform. At the settlement." A look. "The debt is paid, Rose." A pause. "The name is cut." The steadiness, plain as the coat. "I stood, and I am glad to have stood." — Henry

She unties them once more, not from doubt but from the pleasure of it, and runs her eye down the day's entries: the discharge entered in her own hand, the stone's cutting noted, the Park's claiming recorded. The ledgers are closed. The stone stands cut. The house stands hers. The three are executed, witnessed, and filed.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ THE SETTLEMENT — the assembly's set-piece: the three terms executed in ten staged named turns. The debt paid, the name cut, the Park hers — the settlement entire, staged. (Turns: 10 — staged, named)
scenes.prose:
> *(The settlement assembly, staged: the house's great room, morning. The ton's witnesses in their rows, the Park's people along the walls, the Dowager's spectacles at their exact angle, the hawk's delight barely contained, the comte's charm banked, the major's uniform straight, the cousin's courtesy entire, the modiste's bow accomplished, the painter's devotion at work in the corner — and Rose at the head of the room in the verdict gown. The three terms execute in ten staged named turns, the county watching.)*
> **(Turn 1 — The Calling)** *The assembly is called to order — the witnesses, the people, the county gathered — and Rose stands in the verdict gown before them all. The room goes quiet in stages until only the clock is heard.*
> **(Turn 2 — The Acknowledging)** *The debt is acknowledged — named aloud, the sum stated, the years owned — and the ledgers lie open on the table, exact and without shame.*
> **(Turn 3 — The Paying)** *The debt is paid — in the manner she chose: handsomely and publicly, handsomely and quietly, or exactly and publicly — the draft delivered, the discharge entered in her own hand, the ledgers closed. TERM ONE executes.*
> **(Turn 4 — The Witnessing)** *The assembly witnesses — the ton, the Park's people, the Dowager missing nothing — and the word runs the rows: paid, paid handsomely, paid before them all.*
> **(Turn 5 — The Clearing)** *The clearing is spoken — the assembly out to the rise, Hugh's father's name said aloud, the thirty years' wrong named, the stone standing worded in its chalk.*
> **(Turn 6 — The Cutting)** *The stone is cut — in the manner she chose, with witnesses, with words, or in silence — the chisel striking true, the letters rising out of the grey. TERM TWO executes.*
> **(Turn 7 — The Rosemary)** *The rosemary is laid — a sprig from the kitchen garden at the cut name's foot, here and only here — remembrance for the cleared name, the verdict gown kneeling in the grass, and not one voice rising.*
> **(Turn 8 — The Naming)** *The name stands cleared — Hugh's father's name in the Park's stone, legible from twenty paces, the rosemary blue-green at its foot — and the assembly reads it in a silence that is not the ton's usual silence.*
> **(Turn 9 — The Claiming)** *The Park is claimed — hers, beyond challenge: the lawns, the oaks, the stone, the house with its doors open — Rose walking it as mistress at the assembly's head. TERM THREE executes.*
> **(Turn 10 — The Settled)** *The settlement is settled — the debt paid, the name cut, the Park hers — and Rose stands in the verdict gown before the assembly, the three terms executed and witnessed. None present can say otherwise.*
> *(The ten turns hold, and the assembly stands on the rise with the morning's business complete. The debt is paid. The name is cut. The Park is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Gazette's final verdict — Bell's last word on the season, quoted; the ton's-read, the filed. (Turns: 1 — the sting)
scenes.prose:
> *(The breakfast table, the Gazette: the ton's morning reading. Bell's final verdict — the season stated, the settlement settled, the woman unassailable — and the sting is the season's dryness, the independent's, the last word.)*
>
> "The settlement is settled, and the town may look. Miss Hartwell has paid her debt, cut her cousin's father's name into her Park's stone, and made Hartwell Park hers beyond challenge — entirely, and without waste — and the season has its verdict, which is more than most seasons manage in a decade. Mrs. Nance Bell has watched settlements become legacies and legacies become history for thirty years, and she will say this, finally: the discipline showed, the statement held, the wearing was the verdict — and the woman is unassailable. What Hartwell Park becomes now is the next season's question — and Bell will be reading." — *Mrs. Nance Bell, The Morning Gazette*
>
> *(The ton reads the final sting over breakfast. The season is filed, the verdict quoted, and the legacy is awaited. One turn: the reading.)*
